title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026: Updated AFC and NFC standings, bracket, tiebreakers for Week 11
summary: Sunday night's Vikings-49ers game is a very big one in the NFC playoff race.
full_text: The NFL playoff race is in full swing, with the Bills and 49ers currently in the lead for the No. 1 seeds, and a huge Sunday Night Football game in Mexico City giving the Vikings a chance to pull even with the 49ers. We look at the playoff race for Week 11 below: AFC Playoff Picture DIVISION LEADERS 1. Bills (8-1): Heavily favored to stay on top today against the Dolphins. 2. Chiefs (7-2): Have the tiebreaker edge over the Jaguars and Bengals because of a better record in AFC games. 3. Jaguars (7-2) : Their head-to-head win over the Bengals is big. 4. Bengals (7-2) : In control of the AFC North. WILD CARDS 5. Broncos (7-2) : Currently behind the Chiefs based on the AFC West record tiebreaker, but that can change. 6. Steelers (6-3) : Head-to-head loss to the Bengals hurts their chances in the AFC North. 7. Browns (6-4) : Have a clear path to the playoffs. OUTSIDE LOOKING IN 8. Patriots (5-5) : Hard to see them competing without Drake Maye. 9. Texans (4-6) : Running out of time to go on a run. 10 Raiders (4-6): The rest of the season is about developing Fernando Mendoza. 11. Ravens (4-6) : Lamar Jackson's injury just about killed their playoff hopes. 12. Colts (3-8) : No longer competing. 13. Jets (2-8): Aaron Glenn is on the hot seat. 14. Chargers (1-8) : The NFL's most disappointing team. 15. Dolphins (1-8) : The playoffs this year were never a realistic possibility. 16. Titans (1-8): Need to figure out if Cam Ward is their quarterback. NFC Playoff Picture DIVISION LEADERS 1. 49ers (8-1) : Big game Sunday night against the Vikings. 2. Lions (7-2) : Own the head-to-head tiebreakers over the Bears and Vikings. 3. Giants (5-3-1) : Clear path to the playoffs in John Harbaugh's first season. 4. Panthers (4-5): Best record in the NFL's worst division. WILD CARDS 5. Vikings (7-2): Have the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Bears. 6. Bears (7-2) : Their 0-2 record in the NFC North is a concern. 7. Packers (6-4): Have the tiebreaker over the Seahawks based on their better record in the NFC. OUTSIDE LOOKING IN 8. Seahawks (6-4) : Currently have the tiebreaker edge over the Rams, but those two teams still play each other twice. 9. Rams (6-4) : The preseason favorites to win it all now look like long shots to make the playoffs. 10. Cowboys (4-6) : It won't be easy to catch the Giants in the NFC East. 11. Commanders (3-5-1) : May need to run the table to win the division. 12. Buccaneers (3-6) : Still in the race in the terrible NFC South. 13. Saints (3-6) : Still in the race in the terrible NFC South. 14. Falcons (3-7) : Still in the race in the terrible NFC South. 15. Cardinals (3-7) : Have been more competitive than expected, but they're not going anywhere this year. 16. Eagles (2-7) : The worst team in the NFC.
author: Michael David Smith

title: The first 21 chapters of Quarterback of the Future are available
summary: For the 25th anniversary of the launch of PFT, I decided to post the rewritten Quarterback of the Future — one chapter per day.
full_text: '' For the 25th anniversary of the launch of PFT, I decided to post the rewritten Quarterback of the Future — one chapter per day. Three weeks in, 21 chapters are available. The full menu is here , with a button at the bottom of each chapter to quickly move to the next. The chapters are short. Which means there are plenty of them. But each one reads quickly and, ideally, tempts the reader to read the next one. It's the writer's job to make the reader want to do that. If you haven't started, here’s Chapter One . If you like it, click to Chapter Two . I may accelerate the process as we get into the holiday season, possibly increasing to two or three per day. If you want to wait until more are posted, that's fine. All chapters will remain up until all of them are posted. After that, we'll leave it up for a while, if you want to be able to read the whole thing without getting to the end of what's been released and don't want to wait. The whole thing is a thank you to those of you who have been out there since the early days, when we didn't know what we were doing and it looked like it. Actually, not much has changed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Allen is one score away from four straight seasons with 12 or more rushing touchdowns
summary: Bills quarterback Josh Allen has become something that few quarterbacks are — a rushing-touchdown machine.
full_text: ''' Bills quarterback Josh Allen has become something that few quarterbacks are — a rushing-touchdown machine. In nine 2026 games, Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns. With only one more, he'll have his fourth straight season with 12 or more rushing touchdowns. Via NBC Sports research, that would make him only the fifth player in NFL history to have four straight seasons with 12 or more rushing touchdowns. The others were all running backs. LaDainian Tomlinson did it six times. Shaun Alexander accomplished it five times. Derrick Henry and Adrian Peterson did it four times each. Henry, who has 10 this year, is two short of running his own streak to five seasons in a row. Allen's next rushing touchdown will give him 91 for his career, putting him in a tie for 12th all time with Franco Harris and Jerome Bettis. Given that Allen is only in his ninth season, the all-time rushing-touchdown record of 164, held my Emmitt Smith, could eventually be in jeopardy.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaylen Harrell allegedly assaulted rideshare driver before crash
summary: The Titans announced on Saturday that defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Tampa after a "serious car accident."
full_text: '' The Titans announced on Saturday that defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Tampa after a " serious car accident ." It doesn't sound like it was the usual car accident. Via WTSP, the Tampa Police Department said that Harrell was the passenger in a rideshare and that " he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion ." The driver then swerved, hitting another car before colliding with a utility pole. The impact caused Harrell to be thrown forward, striking his head against the windshield and losing consciousness. Harrell was already on injured reserve. Per the Titans' statement, he remains hospitalized. Criminal charges are possible for Harrell, obviously. The driver suffered minor injuries in the wreck; the driver of the other car was not injured.
author: Mike Florio

title: After loss to Virginia, Bill Belichick's bowl hopes come down to NC State game
summary: It all comes down to next Saturday, potentially.
full_text: '' It all comes down to next Saturday, potentially. After a 41-24 loss to Virginia, Bill Belichick's North Carolina team has fallen to 5-6. Bowl eligibility hinges on the last game of the season — an a visit from NC State. The Tar Heels have had two shots at getting a sixth win. They loss to Louisville last Saturay, before falling again today or their sixth loss of the season. Could Belichick's future come down to whether UNC gets to a bowl game? Even with a win next weekend and a 6-6 finish, that may not be enough to get him a third season. He also may not want one, given that the early weeks of the campaign were clouded by the investigations and suspensions and eventually the resignations of G.M. Michael Lombardi and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, Bill's son.
author: Mike Florio

title: Loss to Cincinnati eliminates Deion Sanders, Colorado from bowl eligibility
summary: Deion Sanders's fourth season at Colorado will end without a bowl game.
full_text: '' Deion Sanders's fourth season at Colorado will end without a bowl game. The Buffaloes lost at Cincinnati on Saturday, 35-28. The outcome drops Colorado to 4-7 with one game to play. Sanders became the head coach of the program in 2023. The Buffaloes qualified for the Alamo Bowl in 2024. In Sanders's three other seasons, the Buffaloes didn't become bowl eligible. The loss to Cincinnati leaves Sanders with an overall record of 20-28. His status for 2027 is uncertain, at best. “This is a good — solid to me — football team," Sanders told reporters after the game. "I know the record is not indicative of that and it’s disappointing and I don’t even understand. . . . [Y]ou've got to give Cincinnati a tremendous amount of credit, but it don’t seem like, to me, the better team was victorious.” He has a $25.5 million buyout , which could buy him a fifth year with the program.
author: Mike Florio

title: Knee surgery complicates Puka Nacua's future
summary: Timeline for recovery make mean he won't be 100 percent before free agency.
full_text: ' On Friday, Rams coach Sean McVay said receiver Puka Nacua will miss "a couple months." Nacua is reportedly expected to miss a couple months more than that. Via ESPN, the recovery time following surgery to repair the MCL tear is four to five months . If accurate, that ends Nacua's 2026 season. The problem becomes 2027. Nacua is in the last year of his rookie contract. He hasn't gotten a second deal, due in large part to the off-field issues that recently resulted in a three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy and that culminated in an offseason stay at an in-patient holistic rehab facility after he was " drowning myself " in alcohol. Based on the ESPN report, Nacua won't be back to 100 percent before free agency starts. The Rams will have to decide whether to sign him to a new deal, to apply the franchise tag (or the transition tag), or to let him become a free agent. The injury makes it very difficult for Nacua to land in the Jaxon Smith-Njigba ballpark ($42.15 million per year), even though Nacua's skills and abilities justify that type of deal. The situation becomes a prime example of the extent to which off-field issues can complicate a player's financial interests. Without the New Year's Eve incident that resulted in a lawsuit and, eventually, a diversion program and, inevitably, a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua would have had his second contract by now. Or, at a minimum, he would have had greater standing to hold out (or hold in) until he got paid what he deserves. Instead, Nacua continued to carry the injury risk into the final year of his rookie contract. And the injury risk became reality 13 days ago, when McVay dialed up a running play to Nacua on third and 11 while trying to run out the clock in a 20-13 game against the Commanders. It's a win for the Rams, who may be able to keep Nacua for a lot less than it would cost to give him a market-level contract. However the Rams play the situation, Nacua's knee injury will make it easier, and cheaper, to re-sign him. Ultimately, Nacua may have to prove in 2027 that he is back to full strength. And he may have to get through a full season unscathed to unlock the long-term deal his performances earned — but his off-field complications squandered. Given the way he plays, it's hardly a given that Nacua will emerge from the 2027 season with the kind of performance, and health, that will finally get him the contract he should have gotten by now.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFC North continues its historic dominance
summary: They're 27-10 overall, and 21-4 in games outside the division.
full_text: The NFC North continues to perform like no other division in the league. Three of the teams (Lions, Bears, Vikings) have a record of 7-2 through 10 weeks. The Packers are 6-4. The combined record of 27-10 equates to a success rate of 73 percent — the highest by any division through Week 10 in NFL history. Outside the division, the teams of the NFC North are 21-4. The 84-percent success rate is the most for any division through Week 10 since the AFL-NFL merger. This weekend, the Lions host the Bucs, the Bears host the Saints, and the Vikings face the 49ers in Mexico City. In theory, all four teams could make the playoffs. That would require the fourth-place team landing higher in the standings than the second-place team in each of the other three divisions. And that makes Wednesday night's game between the 6-4 Packers and 6-4 Rams critical to the outcome of the chase for the wild-card berths in the NFC.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aidan Hutchinson wasn't fined for sack that injured Drake Maye
summary: As expected, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson wasn't fined for the tackle that may have ended Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's season.
full_text: '' As expected, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson wasn't fined for the tackle that may have ended Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's season. The weekly announcement from the league includes no fines against Hutchinson. A question emerged as to whether Hutchinson's sack of Maye amounted to a hip-drop tackle. During the broadcast, Fox rules analyst (and former NFL senior V.P. of officiating) Mike Pereira said it wasn't a hip-drop tackle. On Monday, NFL in-house rules analyst Walt Anderson confirmed that it wasn’t a hip-drop tackle . But it's not Anderson who makes the decisions on fines. Jon Runyan makes those decisions. Not surprisingly, Runyan decided that the tackle was not a violation of the rules. Under the rules, a hip-drop tackle happens when a player "grabs the runner with one or both hands or wraps the runner with both arms; and . . . unweights himself by swiveling and dropping his hips and/or lower body, landing on and/or trapping the runner’s leg(s) at or below the knee." Anderson said Hutchinson did not "unweight" himself or "swivel." Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his knee while celebrating the sack. Although it's not clear whether Maye will play again in 2026, Hutchinson is done for the year.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyren Williams has a toe injury, is expected to be ready for Wednesday
summary: Another key offensive player for the Rams is dealing with an injury, but it is not expected to keep him from playing against the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.
full_text: ' Another key offensive player for the Rams is dealing with an injury, but it is not expected to keep him from playing against the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. Head coach Sean McVay said on Saturday that running back Kyren Williams has a toe injury. McVay said the team is not concerned about his availability for this week. Williams has run the ball 139 times for 616 yards and six touchdowns this season. He also has 38 catches for 267 yards and a touchdown, so he's played a significant role in both offensive phases this season. The Rams officially designated defensive tackle Kobie Turner and guard Justin Dedich for return from injured reserve Saturday. The team will issue its first Week 12 injury report on Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: CeeDee Lamb fined $23,882 for block the league used as a highlight
summary: Lamb was praised for the block by the league's website and by Tom Brady, but the disciplinary process said he used his helmet.
full_text: '' When Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb made a downfield block on a George Pickens touchdown catch Sunday against the 49ers, the league's website was so impressed that the highlight video on NFL.com emphasized Lamb's block over Pickens' touchdown. "Can't-Miss Play: CeeDee Lamb's HUGE block springs Pickens free for 39-yard TD," the caption on the highlight video says. Calling the play on Fox, Tom Brady praised Lamb, immediately recognizing it as a great downfield block. But the league's disciplinary process didn't think it was so great. Lamb has been fined $23,882 for what the NFL deemed "Unnecessary Roughness: Use of the helmet." Lamb confirmed to reporters on Thursday that he had been informed he was getting fined, but he insisted he didn't make contact with his helmet and found it frustrating that receivers take hits routinely but get fined when they make one. "I can block, and I'm real good at doing things like that, but I get fined," Lamb said. "I never touched him with my helmet. . . . I guess as a receiver, we can get hit, but can't deliver the punishment." Lamb will surely appeal the fine for what looked, both to the league's website and the league's all-time greatest player, like a good block.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bengals rule out Dalton Risner, list Dax Hill and Dylan Fairchild as questionable
summary: The Bengals may be without both of their starting guards on Monday night.
full_text: The Bengals may be without both of their starting guards on Monday night. They have ruled right guard Dalton Risner out for their game against the Commanders due to injuries to both of his knees. Risner did not practice at all this week. Left guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique) was limited for two days before moving up to full participation Saturday. He's listed as questionable for Monday. Cornerback Dax Hill (illness) didn't practice all week, but a questionable tag leaves the door open for him to play. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is the only other player on the active roster listed as questionable. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm) and guard Brian Parker (knee) are listed as questionable to come off injured reserve. The Bengals opened a roster spot for one of them by placing linebacker Oren Burks on injured reserve. Wide receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb) and cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring) are also on injured reserve, but are listed as doubtful to return this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers waive WR Brandin Cooks
summary: The 49ers announced a couple of roster moves ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
full_text: ' The 49ers announced a couple of roster moves ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City. Veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks has been waived to make room on the active roster for defensive lineman C.J. West. West was activated from injured reserve on Saturday. Cooks had five catches for 58 yards and a touchdown in five appearances this season. The 49ers hope to have Mike Evans back after missing the last three games with an Achilles injury. He's listed as questionable for Sunday night. West had five tackles while starting the first two games of the season. The 49ers also announced that they have downgraded cornerback Nate Hobbs to out for Sunday. He was listed as questionable with an adductor injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers activate CB Mike Jackson
summary: Cornerback Mike Jackson declared himself ready to return to action earlier this week and the Panthers officially added him to the roster on Saturday.
full_text: Cornerback Mike Jackson declared himself ready to return to action earlier this week and the Panthers officially added him to the roster on Saturday. Jackson has been activated off of injured reserve after missing six games due to core muscle surgery. Jackson had six tackles while starting the first three games of the season for Carolina. The Panthers did not activate running back Jonathon Brooks or offensive lineman Brady Christensen, so they will remain on injured reserve for the time being. In addition to activating Jackson and placing safety Isaiah Simmons on injured reserve, the Panthers have elevated linebackers Nick Hampton and Ja'Markis Weston from the practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions place Cade Mays on injured reserve
summary: The Lions placed center Cade Mays on injured reserve for the second time this season on Saturday.
full_text: The Lions placed center Cade Mays on injured reserve for the second time this season on Saturday. Mays has missed the last two games with an ankle injury and he was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers ahead of Saturday's roster move. Mays fractured his wrist in training camp and Mays missed the first five games of the season as a result. Juice Scruggs has started at center when Mays has been out of the lineup this season. The Lions filled the empty roster spot by signing defensive back Nick Whiteside off of the practice squad. He's appeared in two games for the team this season. Linebacker Owen Pappoe was elevated from the practice squad to round out the day's moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders list Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White as questionable for Monday
summary: The Commanders have a pair of running backs with questionable designations for Monday night's game against the Bengals.
full_text: The Commanders have a pair of running backs with questionable designations for Monday night's game against the Bengals. Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White drew those tags. Croskey-Merritt was a full participant in practice all week as he returns from a groin injury that landed him on injured reserve. The Commanders will have to make a roster move to activate him by Monday afternoon. White as added to the report on Friday with a heel injury and he did not practice on Saturday. Center Lucas Patrick (concussion) and cornerback Amik Robertson (ankle) are also listed as questionable. author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles put LB Zack Baun, WR Dontayvion Wicks on IR
summary: The Eagles won't have linebacker Zack Baun and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks for their next four games.
full_text: The Eagles won't have linebacker Zack Baun and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks for their next four games. Baun and Wicks were both ruled out on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Baun has a back injury while Wicks is dealing with ankle and foot injuries. title: Steelers activate WR Roman Wilson
summary: Wide receiver Roman Wilson will be back in the Steelers' lineup for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
full_text: Wide receiver Roman Wilson will be back in the Steelers' lineup for Sunday's game against the Eagles. The Steelers announced that they have activated Wilson from injured reserve on Saturday. Wilson has been out since injuring his hand in Week 5. He had 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns before his injury. Wide receiver Michael Pittman and offensive lineman Gennings Dunker have also been designated for return, but neither one of them was activated for this weekend's game. The Steelers also signed linebacker K.J. Henry to the active roster. Wide receiver Max Hurleman and offensive lineman Doug Nester have been elevated from the practice squad on a temporary basis.
author: Josh Alper

title: Raiders owner Mark Davis hated the Madden movie
summary: Did anyone read the script before allowing the Raiders' name and logo to be used?
full_text: The new Madden movie includes a brief, fleeting glance of a young Mark Davis. The depiction wasn't flattering. His assessment of the film is far less flattering. The Raiders owner teed off on the Madden movie , in an interview with John Katsolimetes of the Las Vegas Review-Journal . “My comment is, it’s full of turducken," Davis said initially. Is that a good thing or a bad thing? “It depends on whether you like turducken or not, and obviously, I don’t like turducken," Davis said. His biggest concern was the script. “I think it’s really it’s unfair to take people that have passed away and make caricatures out of them, and try to sell it as truth,” Davis said. “They start the movie with a statement saying that all of it’s not true, but some of it is, so it’s confusing what to believe.” That's not an uncommon device. "Based on a true story" means that plenty of liberties will be taken in an effort to make the story more compelling. Mark Davis had one specific concern regarding the shading of the truth. He objected to his father's reaction to the serious neck injury suffered by Patriots receiver Darryl Stingley, during a preseason game in 1978. “So John goes over to the hospital afterwards, you know, and really looks after him," Mark Davis said, "and there’s a scene where my dad is telling John, ‘You don’t need to go over there. You don’t need to take care of other teams’ players. You take care of our players.' "That’s just so far from the truth. Anybody who has ever known him knows my dad always took care of people behind the scenes. If it was a player from another team had an issue that wasn’t being taken care of, my dad would quietly take care of that even if it was players on other teams. I’m serious. . . . It just it felt cheap to me to build up John’s image at the expense of my father’s.” Davis praised Christian Bale for his portrayal of Al Davis. “You can’t blame the script on him," Mark Davis said. "He tried.” Mark Davis also didn't care for the characterization of the iconic John Madden by Nicolas Cage. “You know, he at times did look like John, but he wasn’t John," Davis said. "I mean, they made John to be a pussy, and John was the farthest thing from a pussy.” The end result could be a positive. Mark Davis is now motivated to create something that properly and accurately depicts his father. “I don’t know what this movie’s purpose was, to be honest," Mark Davis said. "But you know, it’s making me more and more realize that I’m going to have to put together something on my dad. It could be a movie, it could be a characterization, but at least it’ll be truthful. . . . “I think I need to do that, or at least let people know that I’m thinking about doing that, so that don’t jump in and think that they can do it first.” The concerns expressed by Mark Davis regarding the script raise the question of whether he or the league or anyone bothered to review it before allowing the producers to use the Raiders name, colors, and logos in the filming of the football sequences. That's a critical aspect when it comes to the overall credibility of a film about pro football. If it looks real, it feels real. Unlike other films that didn't secure the ability to use actual team names and logos ( Any Given Sunday , The Replacements ). And that's the irony of this. Davis and the league allowed the Raiders name and uniforms to be included in the film, giving it the impression of accuracy and authenticity. Which, in turn, makes the story seem accurate and authentic. Which makes it even harder to separate the truth from the fiction. Here's hoping Mark Davis comes up with a way to tell the true story of Al Davis. With no embellishment, fabrication, or Hollywood tricks aimed at making the story seem better than it was. Because the story of Al Davis would be pretty damn compelling if it were indeed confined to the strict parameters of reality.
author: Mike Florio

title: Will Shane Steichen be back in 2027?
summary: After the 2025 season ended, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both G.M.
full_text: '' After the 2025 season ended, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both G.M. Chris Ballard and coach Shane Steichen on notice that much was expected in 2026. Then, one day after the Colts lost to the Titans in Week 6, she fired Ballard and kept Steichen. Nearly five weeks later, Steichen remains. After next Sunday's game against the Giants, the Colts will enter their bye. That's typically the best time for an in-season coaching change, since it gives the interim coach maximum time to get up to speed before the next game. Creating a vacancy with six weeks left in the regular season carries a separate benefit. The team can get a head start on searching for the replacement. And if ownership already knows the coach will be fired after the season ends, it makes no sense to delay that part of the process. So here's the question. Will Irsay-Gordon bring Steichen back in 2027? It makes no sense to keep a new G.M. from hiring a new coach. Every G.M. arrives with a wish list of coaches who would be pursued, if/when the position is vacant. It makes plenty of sense to give a new G.M. an immediate vacancy to fill. But what about the Colts this year has made sense? The firing of the G.M. left the team without a seasoned, experienced executive to navigate the strategy of making, or not making, trades. They quickly moved guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. They rejected offers for running back Jonathan Taylor and quarterback Daniel Jones. They moved two starting receivers — Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — on the day of the trade deadline. Now, they've abruptly released Jones. Steichen has been operating for much of the season with one hand tied behind his back. Now, he'll have both wrists secured. Whatever the decision will be as to Steichen, it's unfair to base it on the team's overall performance since the Nelson and Buckner trades. Before that point, they took the Chiefs to overtime in Kansas City. They beat the Texans. They manhandled the Commanders in London. They took the Vikings to the limit in Minnesota. Although the signs point to Steichen eventually being fired, the fact that he's still there now means he could still be there later. The new G.M. may be expected to work with him. It's ultimately the owner's call. And the owner may have strong feelings about Steichen's skills and abilities, based on the fact that she's on the sideline every week. If she was upstairs, she'd likely be hearing criticism of the head coach during the game. Instead, she's watching him in his element. And she hasn't fired him yet. Throw in the fact that a new coach may not be as welcoming to the owner's presence in the bench area, and she may be even more inclined to give Steichen (who's fine with it) another chance. Especially since she systematically began making his job much more difficult the moment the Colts traded Nelson and Buckner. Moving forward, it'll be virtually impossible. The fact that Steichen has survived this long could mean that he'll survive whatever comes next.
author: Mike Florio

title: Titans place RB Tyjae Spears on injured reserve
summary: The Titans have placed running back Tyjae Spears on injured reserve, the team announced.

title: Cowboys place CB DaRon Bland on injured reserve

full_text: ''' Cowboys cornerback DaRon Bland injured an ankle in Sunday's loss to the 49ers. The team had already ruled out Bland for Sunday's game against the Titans. Bland will also miss the next three games, too. The Cowboys announced Saturday they have placed Bland on injured reserve. Bland has totaled 38 tackles and seven passes defensed. author: Charean Williams

title: NFL didn't know Puka Nacua had surgery when agreeing to suspension
summary: The sudden decision of the NFL to suspend receiver Puka Nacua three games raises plenty of relevant questions.
full_text: ' The sudden decision of the NFL to suspend receiver Puka Nacua three games raises plenty of relevant questions. On Friday, a technically irrelevant question was answered. After Rams coach Sean McVay disclosed to reporters that Nacua had surgery to repair a torn MCL suffered during a Week 9 win over the Commanders, Judy Battista of NFL Network reported this: "The NFL did not know Puka Nacua had had knee surgery on Tuesday when it suspended him yesterday." Surely, that's accurate; Judy is a solid reporter. But that extra fact doesn't matter to the NFL's ultimate handling of Nacua. The report creates the impression that, during the negotiations that resulted in the three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua and/or his representatives withheld material information. That, at some level, the league had been duped by the lack of knowledge that Nacua had undergone surgery that will sideline him for "a couple months." First, the suspension (as the league affirmatively explained on Thursday) is separate from the injury. The NFL listed multiple examples of players who served suspensions while injured. Second, whether Nacua (who had already missed one of the four minimum games he's required to miss while on IR), was already going to serve the entirety of the suspension while on injured reserve with or without surgery. Third, the surgery and the extended absence actually avoids the possibility that Nacua would have returned to action exactly one game after finishing his suspension, resulting in no net games missed due to the suspension. The mere existence of the report represents an implicit acknowledgement by the league that the negotiated suspension, aimed at allowing Nacua to double-dip when it comes to his stint on injured reserve and his suspension, underscores the broader question of whether players should be allowed to serve a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy when otherwise unable to play. That's a separate issue for the NFL to revisit, if it chooses, through a potential revision to the terms of the policy. As explained on Friday, the league could have refused the deal. It could have insisted on pushing the issue through the full process, with Judge Sue L. Robinson conducting a hearing and the outcome potentially being appealed (by Nacua and/or the league) to the Commissioner. But that would have entailed a non-zero-percent chance that Nacua wouldn't have been suspended at all. For Nacua, the goal was to get the suspension served while injured. The fact that he had surgery before the agreement was reached gave him more of a buffer than the NFL knew about, expanding the window during which the suspension could be fully served before the end of the 2026 season without Nacua missing time due to the suspension. Which would still allow Nacua to have this issue behind him before the 2027 offseason, when he signs a new contract with the Rams, has the franchise tag applied, or becomes a free agent. Of course, Nacua now needs to tread lightly. The league has made it clear that "any further violation of the Personal Conduct Policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the League." To the extent that the league isn't thrilled by the perception/reality that it allowed Nacua to serve his suspension at a time when he otherwise could not play, the league could be ready to pounce on any opportunity to impose a longer suspension that would apply when Nacua is healthy again.

title: Jerry Jones on fan's death after fight at 49ers-Cowboys game: "We had no record of an incident"

full_text: '' This week, a fan died after falling during a fight at AT&T Stadium. The fan was there to watch the 49ers-Cowboys game. On Friday, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones was asked about the incident during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan. " I just got that information , and so we had no record of of an incident, and we'll be obviously looking into that," Jones said. "My understanding is that the individual went to the game and didn't feel good at the game, and then left, and [had] been hospitalized. But we weren't aware of any incident that involved a fan at the game." They know about it now, and they have the resources to fully investigate. "We really do have quite a — eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago," Jones said. "We have quite a surveillance of what's going on at every aspect of our game. And so it is really rare if we didn't know of any incident. We've got too many people out there. We have 6,000 workers on game day." Jones said he'll pass along any surveillance footage the Cowboys have to investigators. A full and complete investigation could potentially create liability for the venue. It all depends on the facts. And, frankly, it requires the authorities not to sit and wait for whatever is voluntarily provided but to use the subpoena power to go get anything and everything that will allow the complicated puzzle to be put together as to what happened to Marco Narro, whether it could have or should been prevented, and whether the aftermath could have or should have been handled differently.

title: Jaguars saw something in Liam Coen that other teams didn't
summary: The Jaguars identified Coen as their No. 1 candidate and re-shaped their front office to get him, at a time when other teams weren't even interviewing him.
full_text: ' In a season and a half with the Jaguars, Liam Coen has established himself as one of the best coaches in the NFL. Last year, Coen took over a team that had gone 4-13 the year before and improved their record to 13-4 — the best record ever for a first-year coach taking over a team that had won four or fewer games the year before. This year Coen is showing that last year was no fluke, with the Jaguars at 7-2 with an NFL-best point differential of +125. Coen's great success should have other teams that hired new head coaches in 2025 asking themselves: What did we miss? Because the Jaguars were so high on Coen that he was their No. 1 target and they were willing to do whatever it took to get him, while no other team even bothered to give Coen an interview. During the 2025 NFL coaching search , we tracked dozens of reports of head coaching interviews and requests among the seven teams that had vacancies. The Jaguars were the only team that so much as asked Coen to interview. This week there's been some media scrutiny on the Jets, who hired Aaron Glenn without considering Coen as a candidate. Glenn is 5-22; Coen is 20-6. But it's unfair to single out the Jets for failing to interview Coen, because no team other than the Jaguars did, either. The 41-year-old Coen had a résumé that should have made him a good candidate. NFL teams are always on the lookout for coaches who can nurture a franchise quarterback and run an innovative offense. Coen played quarterback at UMass and coached quarterbacks in college before getting hired by Sean McVay to work on the Rams' staff, eventually became the Rams' offensive coordinator under McVay, and had been a successful playcaller as offensive coordinator for the Buccaneers, as well as at Kentucky. With that background, it's surprising that only the Jaguars wanted him. And the Jaguars really wanted him, to the point that they were willing to do whatever it took to hire him. Coen initially turned the Jaguars down and agreed to a contract extension to stay with the Buccaneers, but Jaguars owner Shad Khan wouldn't take no for an answer. When Coen said he was concerned about the direction of the Jaguars' front office, Khan fired General Manager Trent Baalke and agreed to reshape the front office in a way that Coen would approve of if Coen would take the job. Coen was persuaded to take the Jaguars job, and the Jaguars later hired James Gladstone, who had worked with Coen on the Rams, as GM. The result has been the Jaguars going from one of the worst teams in the NFL to one of the best. Coen's success in Jacksonville has justified the faith Khan had in him. And raises questions about the total lack of interest from the rest of the league.

title: Carmelo Anthony calls out Ravens' Marlon Humphrey after controversial Baltimore 'criminals' comment
summary: Anthony spent his formative years growing up in Baltimore and wasn't going to let Humphrey's comments slide
full_text:
Among sports fans, Carmelo Anthony is perhaps most synonymous with New York -- both upstate from his incredible year at Syracuse and in New York City, where he starred for the Knicks . But Anthony was raised in Baltimore and is extremely proud of his roots.
So when Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made headlines this week when he said that the thing the city of Baltimore was best at creating was "criminals," Anthony felt compelled to respond. Humphrey was admonished by the Ravens, which sent him home for the week and will hold him out on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers. He also received scathing responses from Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott and many other prominent Baltimore figures.
Anthony joined that group on Friday with an Instagram post that called on Humphrey to go beyond the apology he issued earlier in the week. Anthony wants Humphrey to join him, Scott, and others in the community to find ways to lead by example.
I've been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn't a talking point to me. It's in my blood. I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take fro you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I've heard every joke and every headline my whole life.
So when one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it'll get cut out, that doesn't get cut out for me. It doesn't get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn't get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner. And it doesn't get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment.
Marlon, I see the apology. I'll take it, man to man. But Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don't build anything. Presence does. I put my time, energy and resources in Baltimore because I want kids to have somebody who believe in them. That's the job when you wear this city on your chest. You don't get to rep Baltimore on Sundays and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday.
So let me tell you what Baltimore makes. We make fighters. We make builders. We make people who were counted out from the day they were born and showed up anyway. We make teachers who buy supplies out of their own pockets, coaches who become fathers, artists the whole world copies, and returning citizens who turn their pain into purpose. We make Olympians, Hall of Famers, legends. We make ME. We make Tank Davis.
The Mayor opened a door. Walk through it. And when you do, call me. I'll meet you there. Let's sit with these young boys together and let them hear from two men who wear this city that they are not what anybody says they are.
Baltimore doesn't make criminals. Baltimore makes the ones who make it out. And the ones who come back. #B-MORE.
The overwhelming response to Humphrey's comments in Baltimore has been to highlight the incredible work being done by leaders to improve conditions, decrease violence, and provide mentorship and guidance to young people in the city.
Anthony echoed the mayor's invitation to join in that work in the community and offered to be there right alongside him.

title: Titans' Jaylen Harrell hospitalized after serious car accident, remains in hospital in Tampa

full_text:
Titans edge defender Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident Friday night in his hometown of Tampa, Fla., and remained hospitalized, the team announced via a statement.
"Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida," the statement s aid. "We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information. At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."
Harrell, 24, tore his ACL in August and has been on injured reserve ever since, which explains his absence from the team. The Titans visit the Cowboys on Sunday.
A seventh-round pick out of Michigan in 2024, Harrell has spent his entire NFL career with the Titans. He appeared in all 17 games in both 2024 and 2025, contributing on defense and special teams. He had 4.5 sacks last season as well. He is the son of former Lions and Chiefs linebacker James Harrell.

title: How to watch 49ers vs. Vikings in Mexico City: TV, streaming, betting odds for 'Sunday Night Football' clash
summary: The NFC-leading 49ers face the Vikings in a Mexico City duel at Estadio Azteca
full_text:
The biggest game of Week 11 -- and arguably the biggest game of the season so far -- goes down on "Sunday Night Football," when the San Francisco 49ers face the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.
The 49ers (8-1) lead the NFC, while the Vikings (7-2) are tied for the conference's second-best record. Not only that, but it's a classic matchup of unstoppable force meeting immovable object.
Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense are coming off a 46-point performance in a win over the Cowboys and have been cooking all season. San Francisco leads the NFL in yards per game and yards per play and is third in offensive points scored per game. Purdy is having arguably his best season, and he leads the league with 9.0 yards per attempt.
But Brian Flores' defense could provide the toughest test yet. The Vikings' defense is second in yards allowed per game and yards allowed per play. Blitzing at the league's highest rate by far, Minnesota leads the NFL in pressure rate and sack rate by a wide margin.
The duel between Flores and Kyle Shanahan is the clear headliner here, but it's far from the only one. Looking at the Vikings' offense against the 49ers' defense, Kirk Cousins makes his second start for Minnesota after returning to the team at the trade deadline. Cousins threw a pair of touchdown passes in his first game back, a 30-10 Week 10 romp over the Packers , and he has looked as good as ever since his 2023 Achilles tear ended his first stint in Minnesota.
The San Francisco defense, meanwhile, doesn't garner the same headlines, but it ranks fourth in yards per play. Cousins and Justin Jefferson trying to crack one of the league's stiffest defenses will be key to this monster showdown, too.
It's also worth noting this game is being played at significant altitude. Here's how the 49ers and the Vikings are trying to adapt.
Date: Sunday, Oct. 25 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location : Estadio Azteca (Mexico City) TV: NBC | Stream: fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: 49ers -3 via DraftKings Sportsbook
How does Brock Purdy fare against pressure? Purdy has been outstanding against pressure this year, leading the NFL in completion percentage (58%) and ranking third in yards per attempt (8.5) in those situations. He has also thrown just one interception when pressured. But Flores' pressures aren't like normal pressures. The Vikings blitz on 72% of opponent dropbacks, by far the highest rate in the league, and when they get pressure, opponents average just 2.2 yards per play, the second-lowest rate in the league. In two games against Flores' defense, Purdy has thrown just two interceptions (compared to three picks) and has been sacked on nearly 10% of his dropbacks. Purdy is better than his past self, but the Vikings' defense is, too.
Will Mike Evans play? The 49ers have been without Evans ever since he left near halftime in Week 6 against the Commanders . The star wide receiver has been dealing with Achilles issues all season, but he's officially questionable for Sunday night, and Shanahan said, "he's going in the right direction." https://x.com/RapSheet/status/2123864564974460973 E SPN reported that Evans has "a real chance to go." If Evans does indeed play, it'd be a massive boost for San Francisco. In Evans' last full game, he had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Seahawks , and his ability to win contested catches would be huge for Purdy against such an aggressive defense.
What can Kirk Cousins produce in his second game? Cousins completely changed the Vikings' offense -- both in terms of structure and results -- in Week 10. The Vikings' 30 points were their most since Week 1. Cousins converted several third-and-longs and gave Jefferson his healthiest workload of the season: nine catches on 13 targets. The 49ers do an excellent job limiting explosive plays, but Jefferson is an explosive play waiting to happen, and now he has a quarterback who can feed him.
This is a true best-vs.-best matchup, but perhaps the least talked-about unit will play the biggest role. The 49ers' defense is truly elite, and linebacker Fred Warner is making a legitimate Defensive Player of the Year case at a position that rarely wins the award. Purdy will make enough plays, even if the Vikings limit the San Francisco attack overall, and the 49ers emerge with a close win.
Pick: 49ers 20, Vikings 17

title: Don't sleep on these three NFL Week 11 games, from Joe Burrow's historic run to a rookie QB encore
summary: Joe Burrow's historic MVP push, Tampa Bay's dominant rushing attack and Fernando Mendoza's second NFL start highlight three overlooked Week 11 games worth watching
full_text:
It's Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season and there's no lack of storylines. This is our final week before the very busy Thanksgiving slate, and it will be make-or-break for many teams.
The playoff picture is starting to take shape, and while we have a lot more football left to play this season, teams are running out of time to make that postseason push as we inch towards the end of the season.
There are some clear must-watch games on the slate, but there are also some underrated games that fans should tune into. Here's a look at three under-the-radar matchups that you should keep up with this weekend:
This game could've made it on my list solely because it was a chance to watch Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow continue his MVP-level season. Throw in the fact that it's also a primetime game and an international game, and we have must-see TV.
Burrow is one of five QBs in NFL history with over 30 touchdowns through nine games, and the other four in the category- Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Peyton Manning in 2013 and Patrick Mahomes in 2018- all won the MVP the year they hit the mark.
The Bengals quarterback is also one of just two quarterbacks (Manning) with five consecutive games with at least four touchdowns. Over this time, Burrow has 20 touchdowns in the air, two touchdowns on the ground and just three picks, with a 78% completion percentage.
Watching Burrow this season is watching history and any chance to watch him is a chance to watch the potential MVP.
At this point in the season, a team sitting at 3-6 probably wouldn't be discussed as a possible divisional winner, but the state of the NFC South makes this a different conversation. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are not that far off from the 4-5 Carolina Panthers , who lead the division. The Bucs have won two of their last three and their last two losses were only for a combined 10 points.
Tampa Bay leads the league in rushing yards per game (163.9), and if Baker Mayfield , who is dealing with a foot/ankle injury, is sidelined, the run game can still thrive. The Detroit Lions defense has a big hole to fill after star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL last week and will be out for the rest of the season. Detroit's run defense is strong, allowing just 90.4 yards per game, fifth-fewest in the league, so watching the battle between a strong run defense and a strong run game should make things interesting.
We are still very early in the Fernando Mendoza era, with his first NFL start coming last week in front of a home Las Vegas Raiders crowd. In his starter debut, the 2026 No. 1 overall pick gave us all a flashback to the National Championship game with a rushing touchdown on a designed draw. His big introduction to Raiders Nation wasn't perfect, going 17-of-29 (58.6 completion percentage), for 143 yards, no interceptions and no touchdowns in the air, against a solid Seattle Seahawks defense.
With those first-start jitters behind him and against an easier defense, it will be interesting to see how Mendoza does. The Broncos' defense has allowed the sixth-most yards per game (355.0), but the ninth-fewest points per game (20.7). They will still present a challenge for the rookie, given the pressure of a divisional game and the road trip to Mile High, a difficult place to play.
The Raiders sit at 4-6, but aren't too far outside of that playoff bubble, sitting two spots out at No. 9. Meanwhile, the 7-2 Broncos would be the No. 5 seed if the season ended today, still fighting with the 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs in a narrow divisional race.
The Broncos are favored, but divisional games tend to bring surprises, and with the added excitement of a new quarterback at the helm in Vegas, this should be an entertaining game.

title: Tom Brady says it's 'obvious' who the NFL's best quarterback is right now: 'Numbers don't lie'
summary: There is one QB who's playing at a higher level than any other QB in the league right now, according to Brady
full_text:
If you want to know who the best quarterback in the NFL is right now, there's no better person to ask than Tom Brady. After spending 23 seasons in the NFL and winning seven Super Bowls, Brady knows better than anyone what it takes to play the quarterback position at a high level, and right now, he says there is one QB in the league who is playing at a higher level than anyone else.
During a video for Fox Sports that was posted to social media this week , Brady was asked directly if Joe Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL right now and he gave a simple answer.
"Numbers don't lie," Brady said. "It seems pretty obvious this week."
After watching Burrow and the Bengals beat up on some bad teams over the past few weeks, it seems that Brady finally jumped on board the Burrow hype train after watching the QB throw for 409 yards and four touchdowns in a 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in a battle for first place in the AFC North on Sunday night.
"Last week, I said Cincinnati needed a signature win, that's not the case anymore," Brady said. "They handled Pittsburgh by 20 on a huge stage, and it was basically over by halftime. Joe Burrow threw four touchdowns without a pick, and that's five straight wins, scoring 30 or more."
The Bengals offense has been on fire since Week 4, scoring at least 31 points in five straight games, which is a franchise record. If Burrow can total at least four touchdowns against the Washington Commanders on Monday night, he'll become the first quarterback in NFL history to hit the four-touchdown mark in six straight games. To put that in perspective, Brady never had a span in his career where he totaled four touchdowns in even five straight games.
During the Bengals' five-game winning streak, Burrow has thrown 20 touchdown passes, making him just the third QB ever to reach that mark in a five-game span, joining Brady (2007) and Peyton Manning, who did it twice (2004, 2013).
For the season, Burrow has been so good that he leads the NFL in multiple passing categories. If you're wondering just how dominant he's been, here's a short breakdown:
To give you an idea of how incredible his passing yardage number is, just consider this: No other QB is even averaging 285 yards per game. Also, he has five more TD passes than the next closest player, and his completion percentage is so high that he might actually break the NFL single-season record of 74.4%, which was set by Drew Brees in 2019.
Burrow is currently a heavy favorite to win his first MVP award, with odds of -125 (the next-closest player is Josh Allen at +370).
As Brady said, "Numbers don't lie," and that's why he thinks Burrow is the best QB in the NFL right now.

title: Cardinals turn to Josh Johnson — fourth starting QB in four weeks — with Carson Beck (back) sidelined
summary: Johnson will make his season debut vs. Chiefs, the eighth team he's taken regular-season snaps for.
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals will use their fourth starting quarterback in four weeks on Sunday, turning to journeyman veteran Josh Johnson against the Kansas City Chiefs . Carson Beck , the third-round rookie who started last week against the Los Angeles Rams , is dealing with back spasms and was ruled out Saturday .
"There is no next step to the playbook; this is going back to the starting table of contents, and that's OK," coach Mike LaFleur said . "For a three-and-a-half-hour window, it's my job to figure out, as you know, whatever we can to get the ball moving forward."
Joey Aguilar , signed off the Jaguars ' practice squad, will be the backup. Aguilar, an undrafted rookie, has yet to see regular-season snaps.
Arizona has endured a revolving door of quarterbacks this season. The season started with Jacoby Brissett as the starter, but he was benched midway through Week 8. Gardner Minshew took over and led the Cardinals to a win over the Cowboys , claiming the starting role in the process. Brissett was demoted to QB3 and, shortly thereafter, traded to the Baltimore Ravens .
In his first start, though, Minshew tore his UCL , an injury that required surgery.
That led to Beck, the No. 65 overall pick out of Miami, taking the reins . He played just one game before landing on the injury report with a back issue, though.
Johnson is on his 15th team (including practice squad and offseason stints) in 14 seasons. He joined Arizona after Minshew went down with the injury, and the Cardinals signed him off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad. The 40-year-old was selected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the fifth round of the 2008 NFL Draft and has bounced around the league ever since, including time in the UFL, AAF, and XFL. The Cardinals will be the eighth team he has played for in the regular season. He appeared in five games for the Washington Commanders last year, finishing 1-1 in the games he started.
Johnson will be the second-oldest quarterback to start a game this season, behind 43-year-old Aaron Rodgers .

title: Cardinals QB issues continue: Beck or Johnson to start?
summary: During training camp this year, both the quarterback and receiver rooms were overflowing with talent and capable bodies. Now, the pass catchers are backups to backups, while the QB room is down to two rookies and a guy who is being paid by his 17th NFL club. This weekend as the Arizona Cardinals are preparing […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 15: Carson Beck #19 of the Arizona Cardinals gestures to his receivers against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images During training camp this year, both the quarterback and receiver rooms were overflowing with talent and capable bodies. Now, the pass catchers are backups to backups, while the QB room is down to two rookies and a guy who is being paid by his 17th NFL club. This weekend as the Arizona Cardinals are preparing to play the Kansas City Chiefs, one of the best teams in the AFC, the coaching staff just might be starting its fourth quarterback this season. Rookie Carson Beck may not start. RELATED: SHOULD THE CARDINALS MAKE A CLAIM FOR QB DANIEL JONES? Beck started his first NFL contest last week in the 34-6 beatdown from division foe Los Angeles Rams. He was scheduled to start again this weekend as center Hjalte Froholdt has been released from concussion protocol. Mike LaFleur: QB Carson Beck had his back spasms flare up. Will proceed as if Josh Johnson will start on Sunday. But won’t close door on Beck just yet. — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) November 20, 2026 But Beck has had some flare-ups with back spasms. Although the team hasn’t ruled Beck out for the Chiefs game, journeyman Josh Johnson is being prepped to start instead. If Johnson does play, that will become four starting quarterbacks in four games. What a QB turnstile. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur stated that the team is taking Beck’s situation one minute at a time, which made it sound serious since he avoided the classic “one day at a time” standard answer. Beck did not participate in practice on Friday while the coaching staff is waiting to see how the young signalcaller responds to treatment. The rookie QB was previously sidelined with back spasms earlier in the season. LaFleur added: “We’re not gonna shut the door on him, but we’re gonna proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is gonna be starting on Sunday.” Beck was taken in Round 3 of this year’s NFL draft and basically was the emergency quarterback for the majority of the year. Then Jacoby Brissett was shipped off, and suddenly Beck was the backup to Gardner Minshew against the Seattle Seahawks. Minshew became injured in that game and then was placed on IR after surgery to repair his () in his throwing arm. Which meant, the next man up. Beck started against the Rams as the Cardinals offensive line did not provide much protection and sacked Beck five times, which could just as easily been double digit numbers. Beck finished going 11 for 18 for 108 yards and two picks, of which one was the receiver’s fault. Johnson is 40-years old. He was a fifth-round selection of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers way back in 2008. The Cardinals are his 17th NFL team. He has played for three clubs twice, plus was a roster member of an UFL team, an AAF franchise, and the XFL where he was the passer rating leader. He played in five games for Washington in 2025 with two starts. Beck was seven years old when Johnson was drafted by Tampa Bay. Johnson has always been the backup, or the backup to the backup. He has played in just 50 NFL games with a mere 11 starts. His total career passing yards is 2,669, what most starters eclipse in a single season. Johnson has a career 58.7% completion ratio with 94 rushing attempts for 481 yards, so he is mobile. I get not throwing him to wolves in this game. Fans would lose interest in watching him play the rest of the year, even with a flawed roster. But back spasms, excuses or not, doesn’t inspire fans support for organization or player. — AZJones (@BrettJonesing) November 21, 2026 Which means he has experience. If Beck can’t go, rookie Joey Aguilar will become the backup with WR/KR Devin Duvernay the emergency QB.

full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The Falcons racked up nine penalties in last week’s lackluster loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, but they were all procedural — there weren’t any flags for actions that typically lead to fines. But that didn’t stop the NFL from issuing four fines total to three different defensive players stemming from last Sunday’s action. Defensive lineman Brandon Dorlus was the lucky guy who got hit with two fines, each for $7,114. One was for unsportsmanlike conduct/taunting, and one was for a late hit on a quarterback. DeMarcco Hellams, who slid into the starting spot opened up by the Falcons’ decision to trade Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars before the NFL’s deadline, owes the NFL $6,509 for unnecessary roughness/a hit on a defenseless player, and linebacker Harold Perkins was also fined $5,203 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet. title: Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 11 matchup vs. Panthers
summary: The Baltimore Ravens will face the Carolina Panthers on the road in Week 11, looking to snap a five-game losing streak and keep their slim hopes of a late-season turnaround alive. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for this contest. Stephen Bopst At this point, it’s difficult to pick the Ravens. They are coming off one […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Calais Campbell #93 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he leads a huddle against the Los Angeles Chargers prior to an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens will face the Carolina Panthers on the road in Week 11, looking to snap a five-game losing streak and keep their slim hopes of a late-season turnaround alive. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for this contest. Stephen Bopst At this point, it’s difficult to pick the Ravens. They are coming off one of their worst losses in franchise history and haven’t had life for weeks. Are the Panthers a great team? No, but if the last five weeks are any indication of what Sunday will be like, the Ravens will again be dominated in the trenches, commit costly pre-snap penalties, and turn the ball over in critical moments. The dismissal of Marlon Humphrey could help the team morale, but at this point, Humphrey really isn’t moving the needle too much. Simply put, there are too many issues right now. Do I have any confidence that the Ravens will magically be able to run the ball, protect the quarterback, sack the opposing QB, clean up their pre-snap issues, and not the turn the ball over? No. X-Factor: Mike Green. Green has been a bright spot on an otherwise underwhelming defense all year with last Monday being arguably the best performance of his young career. If Green can continue to stack games like that, the Ravens could have a future star on their team. Although Trey Hendrickson has been getting a lot of flak from the media, he’s been getting consistently double-teamed and chipped which has allowed Green to take advantage of 1-on-1 pass rush situations. Score Prediction: Panthers 31, Ravens 24 Zach Canter I’m not sure I will pick the Ravens for the rest of the year the way it looks right now. This Panthers matchup might be the easiest remaining on the schedule but with no Nnamdi Madubuike and a drama-filled week with Marlon Humphrey, it just doesn’t fill like the Ravens are in a great spot mentally to go on the road and find a win. The Panthers offense loves the middle of the field, something Jesse Minter’s defense leaves available by design. Chuba Hubbard has been breaking tackles this season, something the Ravens struggle with. The Ravens offensive line doesn’t seem likely to magically improve. If the Ravens win, its because they suddenly learned how to run into sacks against a bad offensive line and because Jacoby Brissett took advantage of an injured Panthers secondary room, that looks to get some guys back this week. I think this is easy win for the Panthers, the Ravens can’t stop Hubbard and the Panthers bleed clock for a fast, low-scoring win. X-Factor: Ja’Kobi Lane. Lane was a favorite target in Brissett’s debut as a Ravens, who targeted Lane 11 times against the Chargers. Unfortunately, Lane only brought in three of those targets and had a really bad drop in the redzone. He was also tackled multiple times on plays that weren’t flagged for defensive pass interference inexplicably. I don’t think the Jacoby-to-Ja’Kobi connection is going away despite the low success rate. Brissett loves to push the ball down the field and Lane’s skillset fits that well. A breakout game from Lane could drive a Ravens win and maybe flip momentum for the season. Score Prediction: Panthers 24, Ravens 17 Yuri Marshall The Baltimore Ravens have lost five straight games, with their last win dating back to October 11th against the Atlanta Falcons. This Sunday, Baltimore faces another NFC South opponent in the division-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5). Despite the Ravens’ recent struggles and internal drama surrounding Marlon Humphrey, this adversity could be the catalyst for one final push to save their season. The Ravens have a favorable matchup against Carolina’s offensive tackles. Rasheed Walker has surrendered 5 sacks and 38 pressures this season, while rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has allowed 5 sacks and 26 pressures. Defensively, Carolina has been a buzzsaw against the run, ranking 8th in efficiency and 2nd when stacking the box. However, the Panthers rank just 23rd against intermediate passes, an area Baltimore can exploit. Expect Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane to see a similar target share to last week. X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson: Hendrickson has an opportunity to deliver his signature performance as a Raven. Carolina’s struggles at both tackle positions, combined with a tight end room that lacks a reliable option to consistently chip him, create an ideal matchup. Expect Hendrickson to capitalize on these one-on-one opportunities and potentially take over the game as a pass rusher. Score Prediction: Ravens 27, Panthers 16 The Ravens’ playoff chances could not be slimmer now after a fifth straight loss last week. However, there is still a mathematical possibility of postseason life — which would pretty much evaporate if they lose any of the next few games. The Panthers are a formidable opponent, but certainly beatable. The Ravens will need to take advantage of Carolina’s weak offensive line and create positive plays on defense via the pass rush. Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson have advantageous matchups against both of the Panthers’ offensive tackles. X-Factor: Roquan Smith. The Panthers have been one of the top passing attacks over the middle of the field this season, which is Bryce Young’s biggest strength. Smith’s coverage in this area has been up-and-down, and he will need perform better in this game. The Panthers have multiple big targets who can catch in traffic. Smith will be targeted often and needs to avoid getting lost in open space. Also, can Smith step up as one of the veterans the Ravens need to be more of an impact playmaker? Let’s see in this game. Score Prediction: Ravens 21, Panthers 20 Dustin Cox It’s hard to imagine the Ravens beating anybody after giving the Chargers their first win of the season. This defense holding both Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan in check seems like a pipe dream at this point, especially without Nnamdi Madubuike up front. If the offense can finally figure out how to run the ball, then this team will have a legitimate chance, but I will believe they are capable of doing so when I see it. Jacoby Brissett cannot be asked to throw the ball close to 50 times again this week, but with how impossible running the ball has felt at times, he may be asked to shoulder a significant load once again in his second game with the team. That strategy worked out decently well against Los Angeles, but dropping back that many times behind this offensive line is a recipe for disaster over any extended period of time. It is time for Declan Doyle to pull out all the tricks to get Derrick Henry going this Sunday. X-Factor: Travis Jones: Jones had a strong game against the Chargers and the big nose tackle will need to show up again this week for the defense to have a shot at limiting the damage from Hubbard on the ground. Jones will be needed to provide interior pressure as well in the absence of Madubuike. Score Prediction: Panthers 26, Ravens 21

full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - AUGUST 18: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders talks with Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals after the NFL Preseason 2025 game at Northwest Stadium on August 18, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Updated Standings: Cincinnati Bengals 7-3 Pittsburgh Steelers 6-3 Cleveland Browns 6-4 Baltimore Ravens 4-6 Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: @ Philadelphia Eagles, 1:00pm EST The Steelers came out flat last week despite coming off their bye week. In a primetime spot with the chance to take a first-place lead in the division, the Steelers punted on four of their first five drives. They didn’t score a touchdown until the fourth quarter, but it meant little as they were trailing by 28 points. Pittsburgh still has six wins on the season, though, and is set up well to earn a seventh victory in Week 11. A matchup with the Eagles is much less imposing now than it was several weeks ago, as Philadelphia has been riddled by injuries and traded away several core players. They have lost seven straight games and the last four have come by eight or more points. To avoid a trap game on the road, the Steelers need to avoid turning the ball over and giving the Eagles’ offense — which ranks bottom-10 in both the pass and run — any short fields. The Eagles have vulnerable defending the run this season, allowing 126.1 rushing yards per game. That affords the Steelers an opportunity to get their rushing attack back on track after Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for 41 yards on 12 carries last week. Pittsburgh’s passing game continues to be inconsistent as well with D.K. Metcalf struggling as the lead No. 1 wideout. Any potential big play that Aaron Rodgers can connect on through the air will be a bonus. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: @ Carolina Panthers, 1:00pm EST Following a fifth-straight loss this past Monday to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers, the Ravens’ season is officially on life support heading into Week 11. The Ravens were unable to capitalize on turnover opportunities, struggled to defend the run, and committed two costly turnovers of their own. They’re now two games under .500 and, in order to keep any semi-possible playoff chances alive, they can’t afford to lose any of their next few games. This week’s matchup against the Panthers profiles as perhaps their most favorable contest remaining on the schedule. There are a couple particular areas where the Ravens match up well and need to take advantage. On offense, it’s their wide receivers versus Carolina’s cornerbacks. The Panthers have been without their starting cornerbacks for several weeks now. They’ve managed to hold up and rank Top 10 in passing yards allowed, but Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane will still have opportunities to win their individual matchups and get open consistently. Given the team’s struggles run blocking lately, the Ravens may be better off leaning on Jacoby Brissett’s arm and spreading out the defense. Defensively, the Ravens need to tighten up their coverage over the middle of the field. Bryce Young’s biggest strength throwing the ball is targeting that area and the Panthers have been effective doing so this year. They have several tall, athletic pass-catchers that have to be accounted for. It will help if the Ravens can create some pressure and convert sacks. The Panthers’ offensive line, particularly their tackles on both sides, has been a weak point. This is a prime spot for Trey Hendrickson to get back in the sack column and for Mike Green to continue his strong run of play recently. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: @ Washington Commanders, 8:20pm EST The Bengals continued rolling last week with another convincing divisional win, defeating the Steelers handedly by 20 points (38-18). Led by another MVP-caliber performance from Joe Burrow and signature showing from Ja’Marr Chase, the Bengals led from start to finish — using a 21-point second quarter to quickly pull away. They will hit the road in Week 11 for a second straight primetime outing, this time against the Commanders. On paper, the Bengals should continue to find success throwing the ball in this game. The Commanders allowed the second-most passing yards per game at over 244 and have a vulnerable secondary. They are much better against the run, but running the ball has not mattered much at all for the Bengals this season. Burrow has been unstoppable airing the ball out to Chase and Tee Higgins, which they will likely continue to lean on here. The Commanders have been one of the league’s most turnover-adverse offenses this season, although Jayden Daniels did throw two fourth-quarter interceptions last week. If the Bengals can force a takeaway or two, it will only strengthen their chances of winning by giving their offense shorter fields. The Bengals match up well defensively with the Commanders but should not let their guard down. Washington has shown an ability to hang around in games and put together late scoring drives.
