title: Browns roster: 2 backups who could help take the offense to another level
summary: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders. There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games. Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use […]
full_text: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games . Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use the bye week to get the team’s running game going and figure out how to help in the early part of the game . Beyond that, the offense has to find more stabilit y, much of which could come through the rushing attack and a schedule with defenses that can be attacked . While many will point to the offensive line, QB Deshaun Watson , and RB Quinshon Judkins as places where the Browns offense needs to improve, two backups could help take the offense to another level: RB Dylan Sampson and WR Isaiah Bond . Now, neither player is likely to take over significantly more snaps for the rest of the season, although Bond needs a few more if he’s going to make any impact at all, but both have a chance to help Monken’s offense be more explosive in different ways. Sampson is not just a change-of-pace back, but one who can make big plays in ways that Judkins just can’t. Misdirection runs, screen plays, dump-off passes, and the occasional late leak-out play could all give Watson and company big gains and keep the offense on the field. Sampson’s ability to make plays all over the field and from a variety of positions makes him a versatile threat that must be accounted for. Bond, on the other hand, has really one gift to give the Browns offense: straight-line speed. Unfortunately, mistimed jumps and drops have led Monken to limit the speedster’s snaps in favor of veterans Malachi Corley and Tylan Wallace . It also doesn’t help Bond’s chances that the top three receivers, KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston , and Jerry Jeudy , have deep route speed and ability, but Bond speed is unique. If Monken can trust the second-year receiver and he makes just a couple of big plays in the first few games coming out of the bye week, Bond can not only become impactful in the stat sheet but also as a decoy. Having Bond run deep post, 9-route, and corner routes can take the top off of a defense, pull the safety away, and create more spacing underneath for all of the above-mentioned players, along with TE Harold Fannin Jr. , to make plays after the catch. Cleveland’s offense will not be decided by the performances of Sampson and Bond, but both backups have a chance to take the unit’s performance to another level, assuming that the line, QB play, and starting weapons are doing as well as or better than they have so far this season. Barring injury, neither is likely to be a fantasy star or steal significant snaps from any starters, but their impact with explosive plays could move things from good to great. Do you think either Sampson or Bond will be able to make a huge impact for the Browns roster the second half of the season? full_text: The Cleveland Browns are entering the bye week with a 6-4 record , already exceeding many expectations for this season. There have been many highs this season, like watching all the young talent succeed and a number of fourth-quarter game-winning drives. Despite all the highs, there are still several areas where the team could improve. One of the biggest downfalls for the Browns this season was the play from the offensive line. It has been inconsistent, and they have struggled to protect the quarterback and relieve pressure in several situations. There have been a lot of sacks, not all at the fault of the offensive line, but there also have been a lot of penalties from that group. The run blocking has been a more consistent concern as well. They need to clean up their play in the remaining weeks to give the offense the best chance to succeed. Cleveland should also look to improve its starts to games to avoid having to rely on fourth-quarter comebacks. Even though they’ve had success with these fourth-quarter comebacks, they cannot rely on that continuing. It will be important for the team to come out strong in the remaining games and score early to avoid having to fight their way back for a win. title: Cowboys passing attack should shine, pass rush could struggle
summary: The Dallas Cowboys desperately need a win, and Sunday’s matchup against the Tennessee Titans offers a chance to get something positive going after all the Christian Parker drama. Tennessee is 1-8 and has one of the league’s worst defenses, particularly in the secondary. Dallas should have plenty of opportunities to move the ball through the […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys desperately need a win, and Sunday’s matchup against the Tennessee Titans offers a chance to get something positive going after all the Christian Parker drama. Tennessee is 1-8 and has one of the league’s worst defenses, particularly in the secondary. Dallas should have plenty of opportunities to move the ball through the air, especially with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens coming off productive performances. There are still reasons to be cautious. The Cowboys’ defense has been a disaster this year, and Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward has improved over the past few weeks. With Dallas also changing its defensive play-calling, this matchup could tell us a lot about the team’s direction. Here are two players to buy and one area to sell ahead of Sunday’s game. Buy: WR CeeDee Lamb CeeDee Lamb has been on a tear this year, and this week’s matchup against Tennessee should give him another opportunity to put up big numbers, so it’s no surprise he’s on this list again. Lamb is coming off a seven-catch, 72-yard, one-touchdown performance against San Francisco. That came after his 10-catch, 195-yard outing against Indianapolis. Through 10 games, Lamb has 77 receptions for 976 yards and eight touchdowns. He’s averaging 97.6 receiving yards per game and has become the most consistent weapon in Dak Prescott’s passing attack. This matchup is appealing. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per game, the most in the NFL. The Titans have struggled to contain opposing receivers, with Cleveland’s KC Concepcion, Cincinnati’s Tee Higgins and Jacksonville’s Parker Washington all putting up big performances against them in recent weeks. Lamb should have plenty of opportunities to take advantage of that secondary. Whether he’s working out of the slot or lining up outside, the Cowboys need to make sure he’s involved early and often. With eight touchdowns already on the season, there’s little reason to believe his production is slowing down. What a grab from CeeDee 🔥 SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TDOobHrr9r — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 Sell: The Cowboys’ pass rush I’m not buying the Cowboys’ pass rush this week, even after the unit recorded five sacks against San Francisco. That might sound strange, but Tennessee has allowed just 14 sacks this season. The concern is what Cam Ward has been doing with his legs and how the Titans have adjusted their offense to better suit him. Ward has been much more comfortable over the past few weeks. He’s completed 54 of 79 passes for 535 yards, four touchdowns and one interception across his last two games, posting a 98.9 passer rating. He’s also been more involved as a runner, and Tennessee has increasingly used tempo and designed quarterback runs to create opportunities for him. The Titans’ offensive approach has changed considerably. They’ve incorporated more no-huddle looks and opportunities for Ward to use his mobility. Against Jacksonville, Tennessee used no-huddle on 49% of its offensive plays, the highest rate by any team this season. That’s a concern for Dallas. The Cowboys have struggled to contain quarterbacks who can escape the pocket, and their pass rush has too often lost its discipline when trying to generate pressure. If the defensive front gets too aggressive and opens running lanes, Ward has the mobility to make them pay. There is also a new wrinkle on the Dallas sideline. Mike Pettine will take over defensive play-calling after the Cowboys removed those responsibilities from Christian Parker. Maybe the change helps, but it’s difficult to expect an immediate turnaround from a defense that has struggled with execution and consistency all season. Cam Ward leads all QBs in rushing yards over last 2 games with 80 yards Him using his legs completely unlock a new dimension of the offense. I know he’s a pocket passer at heart, but it’s clear that Daboll is working with him on this and it’s working pic.twitter.com/B7Z7QbANLi — Titans Era (@titanserashow) November 16, 2026 Buy: WR George Pickens If Lamb is the Cowboys’ most consistent weapon, George Pickens might be their most dangerous big-play threat. After missing time with a hamstring injury, Pickens returned against San Francisco and delivered the best performance of his Dallas career. Pickens hauled in 11 receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns on 18 targets. He set career highs in catches and receiving touchdowns, giving Prescott another reliable option in a passing game that has been productive throughout the season. Through nine games, Pickens has 50 receptions for 678 yards and five touchdowns. He’s averaging 13.6 yards per catch and has shown the ability to stretch the field and win contested catches. Tennessee’s secondary has struggled to contain receivers all season, and its recent performances suggest opposing offenses can find plenty of downfield opportunities. The Titans are allowing the most passing yards per game in the league, and they’ve surrendered several big performances to opposing receivers over the past month. With Lamb commanding attention from the secondary, Pickens should have opportunities to exploit one-on-one matchups. The Cowboys have two legitimate receiving threats capable of taking over a game, and this is the type of matchup where both could produce. title: Cowboys vs Titans: Writer predictions for Week 11
summary: Dallas gets one of its best opportunities of the season to steady things after the 46-40 loss to San Francisco. Tennessee is 1-8 and ranks near the bottom of the league on both sides of the ball. Dallas should be the better team here, but after giving up 584 yards last week, the defense still […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images Dallas gets one of its best opportunities of the season to steady things after the 46-40 loss to San Francisco. Tennessee is 1-8 and ranks near the bottom of the league on both sides of the ball. Dallas should be the better team here, but after giving up 584 yards last week, the defense still has something to prove. When Tennessee has the ball Tennessee should lean heavily on Tony Pollard. The former Cowboy has 628 rushing yards and six touchdowns, and Dallas has just been gashed for 214 yards on the ground by San Francisco. If the Titans can get Pollard moving early, it takes pressure off Cam Ward and gives Tennessee a chance to control the tempo. Dallas has to make Ward win this game through the air. Tennessee ranks near the bottom of the league in scoring and total offense, while Ward has been inconsistent despite showing flashes. The Cowboys need to contain Pollard, keep Ward in the pocket and force long third downs. With Tennessee also dealing with injuries at receiver, Dallas should have the advantage if it avoids the missed tackles and busted assignments that hurt so badly last week. When Dallas has the ball This is where Dallas should take control. Tennessee owns the league’s worst pass defense, while Dak Prescott is playing some of his best football and just threw five touchdowns against San Francisco. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both capable of taking over a game, Dallas should attack downfield rather than becoming too conservative. Javonte Williams still needs enough work to keep Tennessee honest, but this matchup belongs in Prescott’s hands. The Titans can create turnovers, so Dallas cannot get careless, but if the offensive line protects well there should be favourable matchups across the field all afternoon. The Cowboys should have too much firepower for Tennessee. If Dallas tackles better, limits Pollard and avoids gifting the Titans short fields, this is a game it should control. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (5-5) Often a shakeup mid-season sees at least a temporary improvement in performance. I think that will be the case here. Cowboys 34 Titans 23 Brandon Loree (7-3) The Cowboys made a big shakeup this week by taking play-calling duties away from Christian Parker. I feel like the defense is going to try to win this game for their defensive coordinator, and it sets them up well with the Tennessee Titans coming to town. The Titans should be a get-right game for the Cowboys on all fronts, for a team that’s in desperate need of a win. Dallas should have their best performance of the season on defense and should have a strong performance on offense, leading to a 34-17 win before Thanksgiving. Dyllan Rivers (6-4) The Cowboys have struggled against every team this season, good and bad. Considering the game day changes Dallas has made with the defensive play-calling duties, there is a chance Dallas finally takes care of things against a bad team early in a game instead of in the waning moments. But I won’t trust it until I see it. My gut feeling tells me Dallas wins by a touchdown or less. Let’s go with 31-27 Cowboys Matt Holleran (5-5) The Cowboys are no doubt a mess, but this absolutely has to be a get-right matchup for them. With all the issues both on and off the field I don’t have much confidence they’ll do it, but I’m going to pick Dallas to get a win. Give me the Cowboys, 33-23. Mike Poland (4-6) To lose this one would bring shame to the game for Dallas. Sure, things are rough right now for the Cowboys after last week, and to lose this one would be a massive shock to all of Cowboys Nation. Confidence is best described as positive, but skidish. Cowboys win 31-17.

title: What the numbers say about Cowboys vs Titans
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-6 Dallas Cowboys will look to gain ground in the NFC East, going up against the […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-6 Dallas Cowboys will look to gain ground in the NFC East, going up against the struggling 1-8 Tennessee Titans at home. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 343 yards and an absurd five touchdowns in last week’s loss against the 49ers. That’s not a stat you’ll see too often in the NFL. This tied Prescott’s career high for touchdowns in a single game. George Pickens blew up after missing some time with injury, recording 145 yards through the air and three touchdown receptions. CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy posted similar stat lines to one another, each over 70 receiving yards and a touchdown. The defense had a terrible day, yet still managed to sack Brock Purdy five times. The 49ers quarterback had only been sacked eight times on the year before that game. As a team, Dallas finished with 439 total yards, 27 first downs and an 80% fourth-down conversion rate on five attempts. Despite these fantastic numbers, Dallas fell to the 49ers 46-40 . Titans key stats from last week Cam Ward threw for 231 yards and two touchdowns in the Titans 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. Tony Pollard continues to be a dual-threat at running back, racking up eight receptions for 66 yards and one touchdown while also finishing with 33 rushing yards on nine carries. The Titans defense struggled on the day against Trevor Lawrence, allowing 352 passing yards and three touchdowns from the Jaguars quarterback. The Jaguars would finish with 459 total yards on the day. It’s Tony Pollard or nothing The Titans have one primary weapon. He used to wear the Cowboys star. Tony Pollard is the only threat that the Cowboys opponent has on offense. Stop him and you should easily take this win home. Allow him to beat you in the flats on short passes or to gut you for big gains up the middle on the ground and this will be another embarrassing performance by the Cowboys. If the defense was ever going to make a stand and say enough is enough, this is the week. The Titans lack talent everywhere on both sides of the ball. There is no reason that the defense shouldn’t be able to tear the Titans up unless they make mental mistakes, refuse to tackle, and forget the foundations of football. Unfortunately we’ve seen each of those items week after week. Will the be the game that turns things around for the defense, especially with the new play caller, Mike Pettine? If so, they’ll need to prevent Tony Pollard from wrecking the game. What do the numbers mean? Is Bill Murray here? Because this feels like Groundhog Day . Another week against a bad team where Dallas heavily outmatches them on paper. Yet we’ve seen the Cowboys take a lighter to the paper and burn it to a crisp this season, performing to the level of their competition, or worse, time after time. This team will go toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the league in the 49ers, putting up 40 points in a slugfest. But also they’ll completely shut down and score just 13 points against a bad Packers defense. Or they’ll allow 33 points to a terrible Cardinals offense. Perhaps switching defensive play-callers will play in the Cowboys favor this week in a matchup against a young, inexperienced quarterback in Cam Ward. Over the last five weeks, Dallas ranks second in the NFL in sacks. They’ll need to continue that trend and pressure the Titans quarterback throughout the game, forcing him to make errors. Disguises are the name of the game on defense when going up against young passers. It’s not different this week. Team sack totals Weeks 1-5: 30. Cowboys – 5 31. Chiefs – 4 32. Dolphins – 4 Team sack totals Weeks 6-10: 1. Vikings – 20 2. Cowboys – 17 3. Saints – 16 After struggling to rush the passer to start the year, Dallas has improved over the last few weeks. (stats via @Stathead ) https://t.co/ObDnVHbRgb — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) November 19, 2026 Dallas should be able to win this game against the Titans without too much trouble. Unfortunately for us, “should” and “reality” have lived in vastly different universes this year. If there is one last hope for a stress free Sunday for Cowboys fans this season, this would be it. Let’s hope Dallas makes it so.

title: College football draft targets for the Cowboys: Week 12
summary: We’re looking ahead to see who may be on the Dallas Cowboys’ draft card in 2027. Georgia vs. South Carolina Georgia enters Williams-Brice Stadium as the nation’s top-ranked team, but South Carolina has enough speed to make this a useful scouting assignment. The Bulldogs’ front will test LaNorris Sellers and the Gamecocks’ offensive line. On […]
full_text: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images | Getty Images We’re looking ahead to see who may be on the Dallas Cowboys’ draft card in 2027. Georgia vs. South Carolina Georgia enters Williams-Brice Stadium as the nation’s top-ranked team, but South Carolina has enough speed to make this a useful scouting assignment. The Bulldogs’ front will test LaNorris Sellers and the Gamecocks’ offensive line. On the other side, South Carolina has a corner and return specialist whose athletic ability should be apparent whenever the ball comes his way. Georgia: Gabe Harris Jr., defensive end Gabe Harris Jr. has the type of frame NFL teams are always willing to develop. He has the length and mass to play as a traditional defensive end or stand-up outside linebacker. He is not a small speed rusher who has to win before an offensive tackle touches him. He can take contact and hold his ground. His best work starts with his hands. Harris can lock out an offensive tackle and control the outside shoulder. Against the run, that lets him set a firm edge and forces the ball back toward Georgia’s pursuit. He also has enough strength to squeeze a gap when a tight end tries to block him down. There is useful position flexibility here because Georgia can move him inside on passing downs and ask him to attack a guard. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas needs young defensive ends who can survive on early downs. The roster needs another player who can set an edge without coming off the field whenever the opponent gets heavy. Harris would give the Cowboys a power complement in the rotation. He can align outside a tackle in an even front, play the strong side against a tight end and reduce inside in selected passing packages. That versatility would help Dallas keep its fronts less predictable. South Carolina: Vicari Swain, cornerback Vicari Swain is one of the more entertaining cornerbacks in this class because his athleticism appears in two phases. He’s listed at 6-foot and 193 pounds, and he brings genuine speed and excellent open-field instincts. Those traits help him in coverage, but they have also made him one of the country’s most dangerous punt returners. Swain is comfortable when he can play with vision on the quarterback. He closes quickly from off coverage and has the acceleration to recover when a receiver creates early separation. His movement skills also fit man coverage. He can mirror releases and carry vertical routes. Why The Cowboys Care Swain fits the most important item on Dallas’ shopping list. Joey Porter Jr. is the best Dallas has at corner and he’s no guarantee for next season. Swain has the feet to compete outside and the quickness to receive work in the slot, giving the Cowboys options as the rest of the secondary changes around him. His return value could help him dress immediately. A rookie corner selected outside the first round may begin as the fourth defensive back, but Swain can justify a game-day place through punts and coverage units while competing for defensive snaps. Dallas would gain an explosive special-teams player rather than waiting for a developmental corner to become useful. LSU vs. Tennessee Tennessee is trying to stay in the playoff race after grinding out a road win at Texas A&M. LSU has slipped out of the AP Top 25 at 6-4, but its roster still gives evaluators plenty to study. This matchup puts one of the SEC’s quickest cornerbacks against Tennessee’s vertical passing game and one of the nation’s busiest running backs against LSU’s defensive front. LSU: P.J. Woodland, cornerback P.J. Woodland is built differently from Swain. He’s smaller at 5-foot-11 and 164 pounds, so there is no hiding the concern about his frame. What keeps him in the draft conversation is the quality of his coverage movement and his confidence playing the football. Woodland is at his best in man coverage. His feet are quick at the line and he changes direction without wasted steps. He also has enough recovery speed to remain connected when a receiver threatens vertically. LSU trusts him on an island because he rarely panics when the ball is in the air. He tracks it and competes at the catch point despite giving away weight. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas needs coverage talent, and Woodland’s tape supplies it. His quick feet and man-cover ability could translate to the Cowboys’ sub-packages, especially when the defense wants to pressure and cannot afford a corner losing immediately at the line. Tennessee: DeSean Bishop, running back DeSean Bishop has gone from a walk-on with one major college offer to the center of Tennessee’s offense. The redshirt junior is a compact runner and his game is built around vision, balance and decisive cuts rather than rare size or track speed. Bishop presses the line with patience. He allows blocks to form and gets vertical without extra movement. His low center of gravity helps him absorb glancing contact, while his footwork lets him redirect when the initial lane disappears. He is particularly effective on inside and split-zone concepts because he understands how to manipulate a linebacker before making his cut. Why The Cowboys Care Javonte Williams can remain the lead back next season, but Dallas should keep adding inexpensive talent behind him. Bishop profiles as a complementary runner who can handle a series or take on a larger workload if the starter misses time. His running style should fit the Cowboys’ interior concepts. Bishop reads blocks cleanly and gets north quickly. That reliability would make him a sensible Day 3 selection, where Dallas can address the position without spending the premium capital needed at corner, tackle or edge.

title: Cowboys vs. Titans: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 11
summary: If there’s such a thing as a cakewalk victory in the NFL, this Week 11 matchup with the Tennessee Titans could be it for the Dallas Cowboys. The Titans currently holds the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and as such, are considered one of the worst teams in the league. That […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images If there’s such a thing as a cakewalk victory in the NFL, this Week 11 matchup with the Tennessee Titans could be it for the Dallas Cowboys. The Titans currently holds the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and as such, are considered one of the worst teams in the league. That should equate to an easy “W” for the Cowboys. Since there’s no such thing as a guaranteed victory in the NFL, the Cowboys still need to remain vigilant this week and do everything within their power to secure their fifth victory of the season. In order to do that they need everyone to play at their best. Some players have a way of impacting the game more than others, which we’ve identified below. Offense – QB Dak Prescott Okay, it’s somewhat cheating to pick the starting QB as the offensive impact player this week, but that’s exactly what we’re going to do anyway. Dak Prescott should have a huge game in this Week 11 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. The Titans secondary currently ranks dead last (32 nd ) in the league in passing yards allowed (266.9) and No. 4 should be able to pick them apart at will. With the weapons at his disposal, Prescott should be able to slice and dice Tennessee’s secondary. George Pickens could have another big game after last week’s 145-yard, three-touchdown performance and CeeDee Lamb should hit the 1,000-yard receiving mark (currently sitting at 976 yards). Throw in Ryan Flournoy’s clutch catches when needed and Dallas’ aerial attack should be lethal this week. Defense – DB Caleb Downs The last two games have been interesting for Caleb Downs, the Cowboys first-round pick this year. He played arguably the best game of his young career in Week 9 against the Indianapolis Colts, but maybe one of his worst last week against the San Francisco 49ers. Experiencing ups and downs for a first-year player is be somewhat expected, but we believe he will bounce back in a big way this week against the Titans. With Christian Parker losing his playcalling duties we believe No. 13 will be put in better position to play to his strengths in Week 11. Mike Petine will likely have him playing more around line of scrimmage, quite possibly using him as a blitzer more this week than we’ve seen in past weeks. Against a second-year QB and a talent deprived offense, we fully expect Downs to make several impact plays to help secure the “W” for the Cowboys. Who do you have as your impact players for this week?

full_text: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys haven’t been consistent when it comes to playing well as a team, and Jerry Jones made some very direct comments speaking to just that. Mike Pettine will takeover the defensive play calls from Christian Parker, but he insists that they’re working side by side to get things turned around. The safety position in Dallas has been ravaged by injuries with free agent addition Jalen Thompson missing the most time. He hasn’t payed in nearly two months, but that could change in Week 11. Jerry Jones calls Cowboys ‘a bad team’; says team has a chance to play better after Christian Parker’s demotion – Garrett Podell, CBS Sports Team owner Jerry Jones was brutally honest when describing the Cowboys, and feels the recent move to take play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker will benefit the team. “We have not been a good team and are a bad team,” Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, via Yahoo Sports . “At 4-6, that says everything you need to say. … Does that mean we will play a bad game [and] be a bad team on Sunday? Not necessarily. And that’s why we’re trying to improve.” One way the Cowboys tried to improve their ailing defense this week was to strip first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties and give them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. Mike Pettine on taking over as Cowboys’ defensive play-caller, dynamic with Christian Parker – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Going forward, Mike Pettine will call the plays for the defense in Dallas. It was unexpected development, but he and Christian Parker are on the same page. “[Parker] and I spoke about it, but it’s really since then been business as usual,” Pettine said. “I think you see his character and how he’s handled this with poise and professionalism. I had a ton of respect for him before, I have even more now. This is not an easy situation, but he knows as I know having been in the NFL, this is a tough sport for tough people. But it’s something, you know, the bottom line is production on Sunday. That’s been our focus since the move was made, and we’ve been joined at the hip putting a plan together and getting these guys ready to go.” Cowboys injury updates: Dallas’ secondary could get welcome boost with veteran’s return – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Safety Jalen Thompson hasn’t played since the end of September. He has a chance to get back on the field this Sunday. Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson was listed as questionable on the final practice report of the week. Thompson is still on injured reserve, though the Cowboys opened his 21-day practice window Wednesday . He’s moved around well in the three practices since. Thompson hasn’t played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro . Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said recently that Thompson hadn’t had a setback, in regard to a question about the lengthy recovery, and that the injury was a serious one. Brian Schottenheimer Offers No Certainty For Mike Pettine’s Future With Cowboys – Mike Moraitis, Sports Illustrated Mike Pettine will make the defensive calls going forward. However, according to Brian Schottenheimer, his role in Dallas after this season is unknown. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was a guest on 105.3 The Fan on Friday and was asked if Pettine would be open to taking on the defensive coordinator role after this season. title: Broncos offense aiming to turn flashes into consistency
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense are seemingly always under the microscope. Analyzed, then reanalyzed, with hot takes thrown in to make it obtuse. There’s no doubt that through the first nine games of the season, both have been “meh.” Yet despite that, the Broncos are 7-2. Over the last […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos passes the ball against the Carolina Panthers during the first quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense are seemingly always under the microscope. Analyzed, then reanalyzed, with hot takes thrown in to make it obtuse. There’s no doubt that through the first nine games of the season, both have been “meh.” Yet despite that, the Broncos are 7-2. Over the last few weeks, Nix and Denver’s offense have been trending in the right direction. Now, coming out of the bye week, the Broncos need to start stringing together consistent offensive performances. As Nix said to the media earlier this week: “I think even if we were playing great that we would feel really good. I think with the numbers and stats, we will always want more. That’s the thing about stats is that they are never good enough. For us, it’s always about the win column and being efficient and helping our team by playing complementary football. “Overall, during the season, we’ve done that. When we’ve needed to score, we’ve scored. When we’ve needed a stop, we get a stop, and then our special teams are playing really well. Overall, as a team, we are playing well and complementary off of each other. We just need to finish strong. We haven’t really done much yet, so we have to keep going.” One of the most effective ways to help the Broncos offense play better is to run the ball effectively. That takes pressure off Nix and the passing game, but forces the defense to stop the run. In the process, it sets up play-action and the vertical passing game. “I think we can hit them with the variables and run with more conviction,” Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb said to the media this week. “We can do a better job of handling the fronts that we have, and dominating the five- and six-man boxes, and getting downhill, and being satisfied with five-, six-yard gains and getting a little bit more explosive after that. “We’ve done a good job this year of not running too many negative runs. We haven’t had negative one, twos. I know there were a couple last week, but for the most part of the last nine games, there haven’t been many of those. We’ve been on track, but we can definitely do a better job of getting to second-and-5 as opposed to second-and-8 and second-and-9 and be in a better position on second down.” Added Broncos head coach Sean Payton: “(You) reduce fundamentals. All the things that you do as a teacher. … Let’s get more reps at certain things to become better.” For Nix and the Broncos, it’s about peaking at the right time. The next step, especially for the offense, comes today against the Las Vegas Raiders. They had a good game against the Carolina Panthers the last time they were on the field. Now it’s time to stack another good outing on top of it today. “We have to keep progressing, and everyone on the team will tell you that there is room for growth,” Nix said to the media. “I’m not too worried about the things that come with the wins. It’s all about, ‘Did I put my team in a spot to win the game?’” Broncos links

title: Ultimate Fans: THIS is the game to break open the rushing attack
summary: Before I write the rest of the article, I just want to comment on the outstanding play by the Broncos in the Bye Week. IYKYK. But seriously, UFGers, as we preview the Broncos’ first face-off with the Raiders of the season, we have another duo of fans, making this outstanding post double the fun! And […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos scores a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the fourth quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before I write the rest of the article, I just want to comment on the outstanding play by the Broncos in the Bye Week. IYKYK. But seriously, UFGers, as we preview the Broncos’ first face-off with the Raiders of the season, we have another duo of fans, making this outstanding post double the fun! And both of our fans are looking forward to an improved run game, better offense and consistent defense. It is the Raiders with a rookie QB after all. But we all know how division games go, so that Mile High orange better be strong and the crowd loud! And we have the perfect preview from Orange Rush Saga and DBforLife to help us do that! Let’s******* go! The Broncos come off their bye week at 7-2, winning five straight. Denver has had the 2nd-hardest strength of schedule up until this point, per ESPN Analytics, but have the easiest the rest of the season. pic.twitter.com/AspR8odKnq — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) November 18, 2026 Week 11: Broncos v. Raiders MHR – Bye Week is over and Broncos lost a few spots in the AFC thanks to big wins by some rivals. But the schedule should be a little more forgiving for the Broncos. Is that good or bad for this team, in your opinion? Orange Rush Saga: I think that for the most part, it’s a good thing. It feels like it was earned after the gauntlet the team went through at the beginning of the season. I do have a bit of concern about play being softer once playoff time hits, but one thing I’ve learned about this team is they find a way to win in some of the most outlandish ways. DBforLife: Good. We are looking at Buffalo for the top seed in the AFC. MHR – No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza makes his first road start after Seattle pressured him on 19 of 38 dropbacks and sacked him six times last week. Denver has 26 sacks through nine games…is this a prime opportunity for the Broncos’ defense? Should VJ bring the blitzes or let the four-man rush do the work? Orange Rush Saga: VJ mentioned this week that he’s frustrated with the big plays being given up by the defense, so I actually think he may be dialed back a bit. I think he’ll poke and prod to find out where Mendoza’s rookie mistakes show up most and then alter the game plan to fit. In any case, I trust our four guys up front to generate pressure on their own. DBforLife: Bring it. MHR – The Raiders’ rookie QB scored his first NFL score on a 10-yard designed touchdown run, and Klint Kubiak said he should have moved Mendoza outside the pocket more. Anyone who remembers Gary Kubiak’s Broncos knows the bootleg is the family business. How do the Broncos’ best keep Mendoza in the pocket? Orange Rush Saga: While Kubiak said he should have moved Mendoza outside the pocket more, I’m not sure he’s the type of coach to present more opportunities for his rookie QB to get blasted into the next millennium. The Broncos defense hits HARD, and the physicality is well known, so I’m not sure he wants to subject Mendoza to a similar beating that Seattle applied. If he does, though, I suspect VJ will throw Singleton on him in one way or another. DBforLife: Let Ja’Quan McMillian spy on him. MHR – Brock Bowers is questionable with an ankle injury, but he leads the team in receptions (50), yards (676), and receiving TDs (6). If he plays, who is the best guy to cover him? If he doesn’t play, what receiving threats from the Raiders worry you with this patchwork crew in the secondary? Orange Rush Saga: Well, I was hoping Henley could fill that spot. But alas. It’s not a fantastic option, but I think keeping Strnad on him would be the best bet. Singleton gets burned by receivers too often, and Barron has been found flat-footed as of late. If Bowers doesn’t play, though, I think Tre Tucker and Jack Bech could create problems at times. DBforLife: Ja’Quan McMillian should cover Bowers. How about this: Since 2023, Ja'Quan McMillian is the ONLY player in the NFL with: 10+ sacks 20+ TFLs 30+ passes defended pic.twitter.com/H6r2ZDDA6H — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 20, 2026 MHR – Given the above question, the defense did have Riley Moss, Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones all back at practice plus Pat Surtain a few games in after missing three. How much does a healthy (healthier) secondary matter for the stretch run? Who’s your defensive player to watch Sunday? Orange Rush Saga: It matters A LOT. We all love the Devon Key INT in Carolina, but the defense loses a lot of its bite without Jones and Hufanga. I’m hoping that the return of those two will take out a large amount of the secondary’s vulnerability. My eye will be on Moss, to see just how he plays off his big payday and see what we just signed up for another four years of. (And as a side note, I think the deal was fantastic for the player he is.) DBforLife: Moss. Let’s see if he is worth the money MHR – The Raiders have the league’s worst run game(2.9 ypc on average) despite having Ashton Jeanty on the roster. But Denver’s run defense is giving up over 120 yards per game on average. Which number wins out? Does Jeanty finally get loose, or does Denver make Vegas one-dimensional? Orange Rush Saga: I think that Jeanty’s struggles are more related to Jeanty than the rush defenses he plays against. Mike Washington seems to be operating better, but the run game as a whole is not anything to speak of really. If VJ creates an effective containment plan for Mendoza, I think the rush game will be far less effective. DBforLife: Denver shuts Jeanty down MHR – Moving to offense, Bo Nix & Co. have scored 30, 28, and 26 points in their last three games, but four of the five wins have been by six points or less. Against a Raiders’ defense allowing nearly 30 points a game, is this finally the week Denver’s offense puts a team away early or is that just not our M.O.? Orange Rush Saga: I mean… what even is our M.O.? One week the team catches fire in the fourth quarter, and the next week it starts strong and fizzles into conservative play calling after. One thing I have noticed, however, is that the offense is starting to really hum at any point in the game. Having Coleman as the lead back and Bryant back from IR has electrified the offense, and I have confidence that Bo improves substantially as the season goes on. So for this game? My personal prediction is that Coleman lights it up on the ground and control is maintained through time-of-possession. DBforLife: I think we will win by 7. MHR- Sean Payton noted during the bye the O-line “didn’t block very well” and Denver ranks No. 26 in the league with barely 90 rushing yards per game. The Raiders run defense is actually worse than the Broncos’ allowing more than 150 rushing yards per game on average. Does Jonah Coleman break it open? What should the run-game approach by Payton this week? Orange Rush Saga: First: Our statistics are probably skewed by the first five games where the defenses were tougher and the offense was dead(er) Second: Run-first is generally a good plan. I liked the balance in Carolina. Third: Jonah Coleman goes ZOOM! DBforLife: Run Coleman MHR – Sticking with the O-line, Maxx Crosby is never not a problem. Can the line handle him Sunday? He’s 0.5 sacks away from getting 75 for his career. Who on the offensive line has the toughest job Sunday, and how do you keep No. 98 from celebrating that milestone at Mile High? Orange Rush Saga: They’re probably going to put him against whichever Tackle is most vulnerable. So he might be terrorizing McGlinchey (or Powers) the whole game. But! This is a known terror, not an unknown one. So plans can be made… like chipping when necessary and establishing the run to allow the development of Play Action. title: Broncos vs. Raiders: 3 Players to Watch in Week 11
summary: This Sunday, the Denver Broncos take on the Las Vegas Raiders in a classic AFC West rivalry matchup. With an extra week of preparation, the Broncos had plenty of time to figure out a winning gameplan. In order to earn their eighth win of the season, these players need to execute at a high level. […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - NOVEMBER 6: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos speaks to Bo Nix (10) after a failed third-down conversion during the third quarter at Empower Field at Mile High Stadium on Thursday, November 6, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images This Sunday, the Denver Broncos take on the Las Vegas Raiders in a classic AFC West rivalry matchup. With an extra week of preparation, the Broncos had plenty of time to figure out a winning gameplan. In order to earn their eighth win of the season, these players need to execute at a high level. Bo Nix — Quarterback All eyes will be on Bo Nix this Sunday. Nix hasn’t experienced the uptick in production Broncos Country expected in his third season. Through nine games, he is completing just 61-percent of his passes [a career low], thrown for just 1,730 yards, 11 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Coming off an ankle injury, he hasn’t been as productive as a runner, though has added 116 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Over the past three games, the former first-round pick has played better than he started the season. In that timeframe, he has six total touchdowns and only one turnover. Things appear to be going in the right direction, and I remain optimistic he can turn it up in the second half of the season. On Sunday, Nix will face Raiders’ defense that is allowing nearly 250 passing yards a game—a bottom 10 mark in the NFL. With that in mind, I’m hopeful to see more production from the third-year signal caller. Nix has just one game this year over 250 yards passing—his Week 2 effort versus the Jaguars. With extra time to gameplan, I am confident he and the offense will be able to take advantage and put together one of their best performances of the season. I think Nix sizzles in his first game after the bye and starts the second half of the season on a high note. Riley Moss — Cornerback Earlier in the week, the Broncos rewarded cornerback Riley Moss with a four-year contract extension worth $67 million dollars. The fourth-year pro has been a key starter in Vance Joseph’s defense the past two and a half seasons. It’s no easy task playing opposite of All-Pro Patrick Surtain II. For the most part, Moss has passed that assignment with flying colors. The former Iowa standout has a knack for defending passes but has just three interceptions in his career. I’d like to see him start taking the ball away more. Sunday’s matchup provides that opportunity. The Raiders will be starting Fernando Mendoza. Last weekend against the Seahawks, he struggled but was relatively safe with the football. I’m hopeful Denver’s defensive front seven can get after Mendoza early and often and force him into some bad decisions. I don’t expect the 2026 NFL Draft’s top pick to test Surtain much at all. That means Moss should be in store for a high-volume day target-wise. Can he rise to the occasion and make a big splash play in his first game after his extension? We are fixing to find out. Jaylen Waddle — Wide Receiver When the Broncos traded for Jaylen Waddle this offseason, fans across Broncos Country were confident he would propel their passing attack to the next level. Count me in as one of them. Unfortunately, Waddle hasn’t had that type of impact yet. His Week 2 performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars sticks out. However, he hasn’t had over 50 receiving yards in any other contest thus far. Through nine games, the former 2021 first-round pick is sporting career lows across the board. In order for Denver’s offense to take flight in the second half of the season, Waddle has to perform much better. The Raiders have been opportunistic on defense creating turnovers. That’s what they’re good at. Otherwise, they sport a bottom 10 pass defense. Las Vegas has given up the most passing touchdowns of any defense with 22 on the season. They are also allowing the most yards per reception of any team in the NFL. Opposing quarterbacks have the best rating in the NFL going up against their secondary. With that in mind, this Sunday seems like a prime matchup for Waddle (and the aforementioned Nix) to have a strong connection and create some splash plays down the field.

title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 12 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Welcome back to another installment of Future Broncos. We are getting down to the final weeks of the collegiate football season before the playoffs and bowl games begin. Another Saturday, another big slate of games for fans to enjoy. Here are three prospects of interest Broncos Country should keep their eye on today. Sammy Omosigho […]
full_text: Oct 31, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Sammy Omosigho (10) poses for a photo after defeating the Nevada Wolf Pack 27-0 at Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome back to another installment of Future Broncos . We are getting down to the final weeks of the collegiate football season before the playoffs and bowl games begin. Another Saturday, another big slate of games for fans to enjoy. Here are three prospects of interest Broncos Country should keep their eye on today. Sammy Omosigho — Linebacker — UCLA The Broncos tried to make a splash prior to the NFL trade deadline making a deal for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. Unfortunately, the medical review of Henley’s knee wasn’t favorable and the trade wound up being nixed. That saved the Broncos a fourth and fifth round selection in the 2027 NFL Draft. However, it’s clear they are hoping to upgrade the position long-term given their interest in Henley. I haven’t covered too many inside linebackers in this year’s class. However, UCLA prospect Sammy Omosigho is one that is skyrocketing up draft boards. Omosigho started his collegiate career at Oklahoma back in 2023 and spent his first three seasons there. He never earned a full-time starting role in their defense but was a quality contributor in the snaps he played. In 36 games with the Sooners, he amassed 96 tackles, 10 tackles for loss, 2 sacks, 1 forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. For his final season, he transferred to UCLA and has become one of the best playmakers in their defense. A ten-game starter for the Bruins, Omosigho (6’2”, 239 pounds) has been on an absolute tear as a senior. He already has 72 tackles, 10.5 tackles for loss, 5.5 sacks, and a whopping five forced fumbles. Whether it’s stuffing the run, getting after the passer, or doing well in coverage—he touts some of the best numbers of any draft eligible prospect. Given his versatility, I think he is a player Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and the Broncos’ scouts are going to be keeping a close eye on throughout the draft evaluation process. You can catch Omosigho in action today when the undefeated and fourth ranked Bruins take on the Michigan Wolverines on CBS. If he keeps playing at a high level, he should easily be a Day 2 selection next April. Ty Benefield — Safety — LSU This past week, the Broncos opted to extend boundary cornerback Riley Moss. The $67 million deal will keep him in orange and blue for the next for seasons. While Denver’s boundary duo is set for the foreseeable future, the long-term outlook at safety is far less certain. The reason is simple; Brandon Jones is a free agent and has regressed this season. Moreover, Talanoa Hufanga’s contract is up after the 2027 season. Keep in mind most all of their depth players are on one-year contracts as well. There is no doubt in my mind Denver will be addressing the long-term need there in the 2027 NFL Draft. One player that is having a tremendous senior season is LSU safety Ty Benefield. Benefield is the son of Daved Benefield, who was a thirteen-year linebacker and All-Star player in the Canadian Football League. Ty was a backup player and pinch starter as a freshman for the Broncos in 2023 but earned a full-time role as a starter for his sophomore and junior campaigns. In three seasons at Boise State, he played in 41 games with 33 starts and put up some eye-popping numbers: 235 tackles, 18 tackles for loss, 3 sacks, 5 interceptions, 4 fumble recoveries, and 2 forced fumbles. This year, he transferred to LSU to see if he could improve his draft stock and battle much tougher competition in the SEC. So far, so good for Benefield (6’3”, 216 pounds). In my opinion, has been one of the best defensive backs in the nation. In ten games, he has 49 tackles, 4.5 sacks and 3 interceptions. With some injuries in their secondary, he has seen time at both safety and nickelback. That positional versatility will be valued by NFL scouts and general managers and should be of interest to Denver giving the ambiguity at both positions moving forward. His physical profile is off the charts, and he has consistently produced at a high level. I think he is one of the most well-rounded defensive backs in this class and a great fit for Joseph’s aggressive defense. If he keeps dominating, I don’t think being picked in the Top 50 is out of the question for him come spring. You can catch Benefield in action this afternoon when the Tigers take on the ninth-ranked Tennessee Volunteers on ABC. Wayshawn Parker — Running Back — Utah I haven’t covered too many running backs in Future Broncos . I remain quite bullish on the potential of Jonah Coleman and RJ Harvey as the future thunder and lightning duo for the offense. However, both have had some injuries this season and J.K. Dobbins has not looked as good as he did in the first half of 2025 prior to injury. I kind of treat running back in drafts like MLB teams approach pitching. It’s always worth pursuing and better to have and need than need and not have. Strong rushing attacks are what get you through the late half of the season and are extremely important come the playoffs. A particular underclassman that has caught my eyes in a few games this season is Utah Utes junior Wayshawn Parker . Parker started his career out at Washington State. In twelve contests as a freshman, he had 137 carries for 735 yards and 4 touchdowns. He added 11 receptions for 108 yards and a touchdown as a receiver. For his sophomore season, he transferred to Utah and saw an uptick in playing production. Parker had 981 yards and 6 touchdowns on 149 carries. His 6.6 yard per carry average was the best in the Big 12. He caught 13 passes for 185 yards and 3 touchdowns and had 1,166 all-purpose yards. In 10 games this season, Parker (6’0″, 199 pounds) has 764 rushing yards and 9 rushing touchdowns. He also has been more involved in their passing attack under the new coaching regime and sports 29 catches for 269 yards and 4 touchdowns. Based on what I’ve seen, he is one of the best draft-eligible backs when it comes to forcing missed tackles (49 last season) and getting yards after contact. He is a dual threat player that offers a lot of value as a runner and receiver out of the backfield. For those of you who are wondering about his pass protection? It’s quite good for just a junior player. I’m not sure Parker ends up declaring, but he is definitely on my radar. I think he would add a lot of juice and playmaking ability for the Broncos. He has been a big reason for Utah’s success on offense this season. You can catch Parker and the second-ranked Utes in action when they take on TCU tomorrow evening.

title: Sean Payton gives curious answer on Broncos’ vision for Jahdae Barron
summary: With the recent extension of cornerback Riley Moss and the desire for the Denver Broncos to revisit contract negotiations with Ja’Quan McMillian, many fans across Broncos Country have wondered what the vision is for second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron. The Broncos have locked up both their boundary corners long-term in Moss and Patrick Surtain II. Knowing […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 15: Denver Broncos cornerback Jahdae Barron (23) celebrates after a defensive play during a game between the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the recent extension of cornerback Riley Moss and the desire for the Denver Broncos to revisit contract negotiations with Ja’Quan McMillian, many fans across Broncos Country have wondered what the vision is for second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron. The Broncos have locked up both their boundary corners long-term in Moss and Patrick Surtain II. Knowing that, it’s a given that Barron isn’t going to see any significant reps on the outside in the near future unless an injury were to occur. If McMillian departs in free agency after this season, kicking him inside to the nickel spot to replace Ja’Quan makes a lot of sense. Though that’s a bridge the team will have to wait and cross in due time. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton was asked how Barron fit in with the defense. I thought Payton gave a curious answer. Your mileage may vary, but this is what he had to say on the issue. “It’s all year-to-year. In other words, relative to Jahdae, he’s got that flexibility to play in the dime stuff, play outside,” stated Payton. With Denver’s cornerbacks now healthy, it seems likely, based off the aforementioned, that Barron’s only chance of seeing the field this year [barring injury] is going to be in Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph’s dime packages. That’s not necessarily the news Broncos Country wants to hear, with many of them longing for the 2025 first-round pick to have a larger role in the defense. Moving forward, as noted, things do remain fluid. On multiple occasions, Payton and Joseph have touted Barron’s outside and inside flexibility. One thought that has rolled through my mind, as well as many of yours, is whether or not Jahdae could have a future at the safety position—potentially replacing Brandon Jones, who is a free agent at the end of this season. Back when Payton was coaching the New Orleans Saints, they drafted Ohio State standout Malcolm Jenkins in the first round of the 2009 NFL Draft. Like Barron, Jenkins was also a Jim Thorpe Award winner. During his rookie season, he spent time on the boundary but had most of his snaps inside at the nickel in Gregg Williams’ defense. The following year, he would move to free safety, a position he would man for the Saints and Philadelphia Eagles for the next twelve years of his career. Asked as a follow up to the first question, Payton gave his answer on Barron’s ability to play safety. He kept it short and sweet. “That’s not something we’ve thought about or discussed.” All things considered, I am a bit surprised by Payton’s answer. Though the fluidity with the year-to-year comment does make a bit of sense. Given Barron’s versatility and ability to play multiple roles, he’s a good player to have in the defense. But the commentary given by Payton makes it a little ambiguous as to what the future has in store for Barron. For now, apparently Barron will be relegated to dime package looks. Beyond this season? That’ll be determined with whatever moves they make in the offseason. What do you think, Broncos Country? Give me your thoughts on Payton’s comments and where you see Barron fitting in with the team moving forward.

title: Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Detroit Lions preview: 4 key stats
summary: The Detroit Lions (7-2) enter Week 11 riding a five-game winning streak, their longest since early 2024. They’ll need to keep stacking wins to stay competitive with the NFC’s top teams, as several continue to add victories. This Sunday, the Lions will host the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who continue to fight for the top […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Sam LaPorta #87 of the Detroit Lions runs the ball during the NFL 2025 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (7-2) enter Week 11 riding a five-game winning streak, their longest since early 2024. They’ll need to keep stacking wins to stay competitive with the NFC’s top teams, as several continue to add victories. This Sunday, the Lions will host the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who continue to fight for the top seed in the NFC South, a division in which every team has a losing record. The two teams have met four times in the last three seasons, including in the 2023 Playoffs, with Detroit winning three of those games. In fact, Detroit’s only blemish came early in 2024, the game before the Lions’ previously mentioned extended winning streak. The Buccaneers enter this matchup with Baker Mayfield trending toward starting after his availability was initially in serious doubt. Mayfield, who already missed Weeks 4-6 with a thumb injury, has also dealt with a plantar fascia injury that required time in a walking boot. Mayfield won’t be the only familiar face returning to Ford Field as a slew of former Lions now play on the Buccaneers’ defense, including Alex Anzalone, Al-Quadin Muhammad, Ifeatu Melifonwu, A’Shawn Robinson, and Miles Killebrew. While Mayfield appears poised to suit up, his mounting injuries and inconsistent play this season leave plenty of questions surrounding the Buccaneers’ offense. Instead, this Week 11 preview will focus on the heavyweight bout between the Lions’ offense and a Buccaneers defense playing like a dominant top-10 unit for the first time since 2023. Tampa Bay enters the matchup well-rested after its bye week, while Detroit heads straight back into action after its international trip to Germany. With several familiar faces on the other side of the ball, it should be a physical, hard-hitting battle in the trenches between two units looking to impose their will. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. The Vikings’ Pirate Cousins Having already faced the Minnesota Vikings’ defense, the Detroit Lions’ offense should feel somewhat prepared for the high-seas approach Bucs coach Todd Bowles’ defense employs: heavy blitzing and plenty of zone coverage. With a league-leading -0.21 EPA/play and the second-best 24.9% stuff rate, the Bucs blitz on 42.0% of snaps, behind only the Vikings. That’s the third-highest blitz rate of any team over the last three seasons, behind only the 2025 and 2026 Vikings. Tampa Bay also plays zone coverage at an 81.4% rate (7th). The Buccaneers’ defense is terrific against the run and will make it challenging for the Lions to grind it out on the ground. As much of this preview will emphasize, Detroit may need to put the game on Jared Goff’s shoulders. Staying ahead of the sticks won’t come easily, and the Lions will likely face numerous crucial third downs. Nobody deploys more third-down zone blitzes than Todd Bowles; the Buccaneers lead the league, facing 26 third-down dropbacks while running them. Opponents are just 8-of-22 passing for 74 yards (3.36 YPA), with three sacks and one interception against Tampa Bay’s third-down zone blitzes. They excel at getting off the field. It’s even worse on third-and-long (7-plus yards), where opponents have faced 11 dropbacks and completed just 1-of-8 passes for one yard, with two sacks, 10 pressures, and zero first downs. Overall, when running zone blitzes on third down, the Buccaneers lead the league in pressure rate (61.5%), while allowing a league-low first-down rate (15.4%) and EPA/dropback (-1.183). They’re particularly problematic at ending opponents’ drives with this tactic. Luckily, the Lions have a slew of options to find solutions against zone blitzes this season: Amon-Ra St. Brown: 20 targets, 17 catches, 178 receiving yards, 10 first downs Sam LaPorta: 14 targets, 12 catches, 157 receiving yards, 6 first downs Jameson Williams: 12 targets, 9 receptions, 112 receiving yards, 7 first downs Jahmyr Gibbs: 10 targets, 9 receptions, 113 receiving yards, 4 first downs That’s a good crew of problem-solving playmakers. Much of the Lions’ success on Sunday will depend on Goff’s ability to process the chaos and find his dudes, along with Juice Scruggs helping Goff sort out the protection schemes and keep the Buccaneers’ pressure packages from wreaking havoc. An Extra Tight End to Sink the Ship Brock Wright is one of the few remaining sixth-year players under Dan Campbell, and he had the third-longest catch of his career (29 yards) against the Buccaneers in the 2023 Divisional Round playoffs. His usage, alongside Sam LaPorta, could be a key factor in this matchup. The Lions’ offense utilizes 12-personnel on 34.2% of plays, the third-most in the league. They rank outside the top 12 in every EPA metric (per play, dropback, and rush), as well as passing success rate, but have managed a 46.0% rushing success rate (8th) and 3.24 yards after contact per rush (3rd). With 13-personnel being all the rage this season, the Lions have leaned into it more, but they still rely heavily on 12-personnel despite its relative inefficiency. Finding solutions with LaPorta and Wright on the field might be one of the best ways to attack the Buccaneers’ defense. The Buccaneers have the league’s best defense against 11-personnel (-0.296 EPA/play) and the second-best against 13-personnel (-0.178 EPA/play). However, when facing 12-personnel, they rank 20th in EPA/play (+0.017) and 26th in success rate (48.6%). Despite being an aggressive and physical defense, with two behemoths in the middle in defensive tackles Vita Vea and A’Shawn Robinson, along with rookie thumper Josiah Trotter at linebacker, the Buccaneers struggle when an offense goes bigger and brings that second tight end onto the field. The Buccaneers respond to 12-personnel with their base defense on 77.5% of snaps (4th), and they’re most susceptible when matching with base personnel, which keeps rookie Keionte Scott, a favorite draft prospect among Lions fans, on the sideline. In those situations, Tampa Bay’s defense is allowing +0.116 EPA/play (28th) and a 51.4% success rate (28th). All of a sudden, they go from a top-five defense to a bottom-five defense. It’s one way to cut the fuse on the Buccaneers’ cannonball defense. Defending the run from base against 12 personnel, the Buccaneers have faced 46 rushes. Among 28 teams that have faced at least 15 rushing plays in that scenario, they rank 19th in EPA/rush (-0.056) and 18th in rushing success rate allowed (41.3%). The drop-off is even more dramatic against the pass. On 61 such dropbacks, among 26 teams that have faced at least 15 dropbacks in that situation, Tampa Bay is allowing +0.245 EPA/dropback (20th) and a 59.0% passing success rate (24th). Opposing offenses are also completing 69.0% of their passes (20th) and averaging 9.21 yards per pass attempt (21st). In those situations, the Buccaneers are still bringing the heat, blitzing on 55.7% of dropbacks (8th), but generating pressure on only 32.8% of dropbacks (18th) and producing a lowly 3.3% sack rate (22nd). Add in the fact that the Buccaneers must overcome the absence of safety Antoine Winfield Jr., with Melifonwu filling in alongside Tykee Smith, leaving Tampa Bay’s defense ripe for Goff and offensive coordinator Drew Petzing to pepper through the passing game. Baiting the Buccaneers One way to take command of the seas and commandeer the Buccaneers’ defensive vessel is by using those extra tight ends in accordance with maritime play-action law. Against offenses utilizing 12-personnel and 13-personnel, the Buccaneers’ defense has shown some vulnerabilities, and opponents have taken notice. Tampa Bay has faced 52 play-action dropbacks with those extra tight…

title: Detroit Lions place Cade Mays on IR, re-sign CB to active roster
summary: The Detroit Lions have placed prized free-agent center Cade Mays on injured reserve with an ankle injury, his second stint on IR this season. In a corresponding move, the Lions re-signed corner Nick Whiteside to the active roster and have also elevated linebacker Owen Pappoe for their Week 11 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. […]
full_text: Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) looks on during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions have placed prized free-agent center Cade Mays on injured reserve with an ankle injury, his second stint on IR this season. In a corresponding move, the Lions re-signed corner Nick Whiteside to the active roster and have also elevated linebacker Owen Pappoe for their Week 11 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Mays signed a three-year, $25 million contract with the Lions this offseason, but he’s had a difficult, injury-plagued first season. After breaking his wrist in training camp, Mays spent the first six weeks on injured reserve before finally returning to action in Week 7. In Week 8, Mays injured his ankle in the first half of the Lions game with the Vikings and could not return. While initially deemed a “low ankle sprain,” Mays was only projected to miss 1-6 weeks. With that prognosis, it wasn’t surprising that he was kept on the active roster and ruled OUT for Weeks 9 and 10, as a return seemed possible in the coming weeks. However, now that he has been placed on injured reserve, he must miss the next four games (Weeks 11-14) and is not eligible to return to the active roster until Week 15 (ironically against the Vikings) at the earliest. If his ankle injury is the “high” variety, his season could already be over, but we’ll need to wait for an update from coach Dan Campbell before we know more. With Mays now out for the foreseeable future, the Lions will continue to lean on Juice Scruggs, who has been terrific as an injury replacement. Scruggs is having a career year in Detroit and looks like a perfect fit for the system and culture. Behind Scruggs on the depth chart is Seth McLaughlin, who has only seen time this season in garbage-time/clock-killing situations and on special teams. Whiteside was released from the active roster earlier this week when the Lions claimed EDGE Tyrus Wheat off waivers, then re-signed him to the practice squad on Wednesday. Now, three days later, he is back on the active roster, providing depth at a secondary that is getting healthier every day, as well as on special teams. Pappoe has now been elevated for the second week in a row, after contributing on special teams in Week 10 against the Patriots. Expectations are that he will fill the same role against the Bucs.

title: Packers re-sign RB Pierre Strong Jr.
summary: The Green Bay Packers, as expected, have re-signed running back Pierre Strong Jr. to the practice squad on Saturday after no team claimed him on waivers. Strong, who started the season on the practice squad, was elevated to the active roster while the team was dealing with injuries and Josh Jacobs’ stint on the exempt […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers, as expected, have re-signed running back Pierre Strong Jr. to the practice squad on Saturday after no team claimed him on waivers. Strong, who started the season on the practice squad, was elevated to the active roster while the team was dealing with injuries and Josh Jacobs’ stint on the exempt list. With four running backs on the active roster moving forward, Strong was the odd man out in the group. He’s just the second player released from the Packers’ 53-man roster, after receiver Coleman Owen — who was let go and then later re-signed to the practice squad last week. Based on this transaction, the Packers are over-signed on the practice squad right now, so expect a corresponding roster move (a release from the practice squad) to be made soon. Here are the current players on the practice squad: QB: Cam Miller RB: Pierre Strong Jr. WR: Coleman Owen, Isaiah Neyor and Quincy Skinner Jr. TE: Drake Dabney and Kenny Fletcher Jr. OL: Dalton Cooper and Dillon Wade DL: Mazi Smith and Haggai Ndubuisi (international exemption) ED: Arron Mosby, Nyjalik Kelly and D.J. Johnson LB: Jack Dingle CB: Domani Jackson and Elijah Culp S: John Saunders Jr. K: None P: None LS: None My guess is that the Packers will end up letting go of a player at a position where they’re over-signed, like tight end, edge defender or cornerback. Usually, they like to have at least one practice squad body in every core position group. Johnson was in practice on Saturday, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky , which means that the missing player was likely released already, even if the move hasn’t officially been announced.

title: Packers Injuries: Entire roster healthy enough to practice on Saturday
summary: The Green Bay Packers have an odd schedule this week, as the team prepares for a Wednesday night game against the Los Angeles Rams, coming off a bye week. The Packers’ players got back on Friday, following three days off after the team “flushed,” in the words of head coach Matt LaFleur, their game against […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have an odd schedule this week, as the team prepares for a Wednesday night game against the Los Angeles Rams, coming off a bye week. The Packers’ players got back on Friday, following three days off after the team “flushed,” in the words of head coach Matt LaFleur, their game against the Minnesota Vikings on Monday. Here’s the good news: Every single player on the Packers’ 53-man roster was active in practice today, at least in limited fashion. Yes, that means receivers Skyy Moore and Bo Melton and cornerback Brandon Cisse, who were unable to finish the game against the Vikings, were suited up for action on Saturday. On top of that, players like running back Josh Jacobs, center Sean Rhyan, guard Kevin Zeitler and linebacker Zaire Franklin were also able to get looks, after not playing at all against the Vikings. The Packers are not releasing an official injury report today — meaning we’ll only get two of these before the team travels to Los Angeles on Tuesday. Jacobs, coming off surgery for a fractured finger, is wearing a cast around his fingers in practice right now. Everyone on the active roster practiced on Saturday, along with EDGE Micah Parsons That means LB Zaire Franklin, C Sean Rhyan, WR Skyy Moore, CB Brandon Cisse, WR Bo Melton, G Kevin Zeitler, & RB Josh Jacobs were all back. Jacobs wearing a claw-like cast on his fingers pic.twitter.com/rwIi4HBtkC — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) November 21, 2026 Left tackle Jordan Morgan also appears to have a cast on his left wrist, based on practice video. It’s the little things. pic.twitter.com/teDZAkrDjK — Bill Huber (@BillHuberNFL) November 21, 2026 Based on the individual drills portion of practice that the media is available for, it looks like the open right guard competition is starting out with both Aaron Banks and Kevin Zeitler sharing reps at the position this week. Last week, Banks was on the bench, as he was dealing with two injuries, while Zeitler was injured during the team’s Thursday practice and couldn’t go against Minnesota. So Travis Glover, who made the start at right guard last week, appears to be the third option at the position going into Rams week. It’s also worth noting that on the offensive line John Williams, the team’s third-string center, got the start, but Sean Rhyan is now in that role in practice — a sign he’ll be able to play in the upcoming game.

title: Packers should lean on running back Kaleb Johnson after their bye
summary: The bright spots of the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings are few and far between, but running back Kaleb Johnson was surely among them. “I thought he did a nice job,” LaFleur said of Johnson’s 10-carry, 42-yard outing. “I liked how he was hitting the hole, running with good pad level, pressing the […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - NOVEMBER 15: Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) is tackled for a loss during a game between the Green Bay Packers and the Minnesota Vikings on November 15, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The bright spots of the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings are few and far between, but running back Kaleb Johnson was surely among them. “I thought he did a nice job,” LaFleur said of Johnson’s 10-carry, 42-yard outing. “I liked how he was hitting the hole, running with good pad level, pressing the line of scrimmage. I thought that was a positive performance.” If there’s a big takeaway to be had here, it’s that Johnson should be getting the lion’s share of carries going forward, and probably deserves more snaps, too. Josh Jacobs remains a mystery. He’s on track to return in relatively short order from finger surgery, but a potential suspension still looms like the sword of Damocles. He wasn’t overly effective as a runner in his brief return to the lineup, either. Across three games, Jacobs carried 36 times for just 80 yards, an abysmal 2.2 yards per carry. Even the perpetually disappointing MarShawn Lloyd has managed 2.7 yards per attempt this year. Speaking of Lloyd, even if he’s better than Jacobs this year, he’s obviously not the future or the present at the position. Kudos to him for making it all the way back from his various injury issues over the last couple of seasons, but it’s abundantly clear he can’t get the job done. It’s hard to foresee him improving much even if the Packers make major strides on the offensive line. Chris Brooks, meanwhile, is a solid but limited player. It’s probably better to think of him as a fullback at this point, a latter day John Kuhn who mostly finds his way to the field because he’s not going to screw it up for the Packers in pass protection. And since Pierre Strong Jr. has now been released, that leaves us with Johnson as the last remaining back on the roster, and perhaps the most viable. The big problem with Johnson to this point has been his limited value in the passing game. You can see what the Packers think of him there by just look at his snap usage. He was on the field for 13 snaps against the Vikings and carried the ball on 10 of them. As a rule, they don’t want him catching passes or blocking for Jordan Love. But LaFleur did call out Johnson’s pass blocking as his most notable contribution on Sunday. Johnson stonewalled a blitzing linebacker on a 19-yard completion. “The thing I was most pleased with was one of the protections when we hit [Tucker Kraft], he came across and picked up Eric Wilson on the blitz right in the B gap,” LaFleur said. You don’t have to be a tape grinder to see what LaFleur is talking about . Johnson lines up to Jordan Love’s left on the play, but alertly comes across the formation to pick off Wilson just as he jets past Travis Glover. Love completes the pass to Kraft, and the Packers would go on to score three points on the drive, cutting the Vikings’ lead to just 10 points. In theory, it could have been a pivotal play. The fact is that Johnson is the only back doing anything even close to making pivotal plays this season. The Packers have only had a back rush for 40 or more yards in a game three times this season, and Johnson is responsible for all three of those occurrences. The Packers will probably never have a good running game this season, but if they’re going to do anything at all on the ground, it’s probably going to be because Johnson is getting the work done.
