title: The Day After the Day After: Houston Texans stomp the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night
summary: The Textbook Texans’ Sequence: If the Texans could script their ideal game sequence, look no further than what happened between the 11:55 and 4:19 marks of the 3rd Quarter. It started with Kai Kroeger, whose punting has been sporadic at best, uncorking a 56-yard punt that landed out of bounds at the IND 5. This […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Jadeveon Clowney #90 of the Houston Texans celebrates with Will Anderson Jr. #51 after sacking Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts during the second quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Textbook Texans’ Sequence: If the Texans could script their ideal game sequence, look no further than what happened between the 11:55 and 4:19 marks of the 3rd Quarter. It started with Kai Kroeger, whose punting has been sporadic at best, uncorking a 56-yard punt that landed out of bounds at the IND 5. This put the Colts in bad field position, allowing the Texans’ defense to go on the attack. Two plays yielded only 2 yards for the Colts. On 3rd and long, the Colts wisely thought to double Will Anderson Jr. However, Anderson soundly beat that double team, all but driving the tackle right into Jones, as Anderson turned that sack into a safety. On the subsequent possession, Houston used a Smith 32-yard kick return to start at their 43. From there, Houston used a 10-play (6 run/4 pass), 57-yard drive that took over 6 minutes off the clock and ended in a TD that put the Texans up 23. Strong special teams, dominant defense and a steady, scoring offense. When a team is 4-6, that usually means the ideal hasn’t happened a lot. The End of the Jones Era: The Texans’ defense beating of the Colts was so severe, it reverberated beyond the gridiron. As the second half wore on, sideline cameras showed visible frustration between QB Daniel Jones and HC Shane Steichen, as the Colts proved unable to move the ball. After an 87-yard, 3-point 1st quarter, the Colts only managed 80 yards and no points over the next 3. On the Colts’ final offensive possession, Jones gave way to Anthony Richardson. Might the Colts face a QB controversy for their next game? Guess not. Not 18 hours after the final whistle in Houston, the Colts announced they cut Daniel Jones. The same QB who led them to an 8-2 start last season and whom was signed to a 2-year/$88M contract this past offseason. The same QB who the Colts did not want to ship to Minnesota or Baltimore before last week’s trade deadline, who would have offered some draft compensation. Granted, the Colts’ season is the road to nowhere, but this sort of move only amplifies the missteps the planning of the franchise. They do save some cap space, but this only amplifies matters. THE CRITICAL PLAY: 3:54, 1nd Quarter, 2nd and 10, IND Ball @ the HOU 38; Daniel Jones pass intended for TE Tyler Warren incomplete (pass defended by LB Jake Hansen). At this point in the game, the Colts led the Texans 3-0 and had just ended up with a rather silly but effective interception. Mainly on the strength of a 26-yard pass play from Jones to Quez Watkins, the Colts were again in scoring position in HOU territory. After a short incompletion on 1st and 10, Jones was again in a shotgun set, taking the snap. TE Warren, the Colts most dangerous receiver at this point, lined up on the offensive right side and was running an in-breaking route that would have netted at least a Colts’ first down closer to the Houston red zone. However, the LB in coverage, Hansen, read the play and got his hand out to deflect the pass. This allowed Houston to force the Colts into an obvious pass play. After another incompletion, the Colts settled for a long FG, which they missed. Houston then scored on three of the next four possessions to take complete control of the game. Had the Colts made that completion, maybe they only go up 6-0, but they would have taken greater control. Houston, already under immense pressure from the implosion in Cleveland, might have pressed too much, leading to even more mistakes. Likely this Colts’ team wasn’t winning on Thursday but had Jones thrown that pass to where Warren could get it for a good completion, momentum might have favored the Colts even more. For Houston, a team that seems to produce more bad luck for itself than good, they got some good fortune for once. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 3: Stroud’s consecutive game streak for a number of stats: CJ Stroud’s done all of the following over the past three games: Thrown an INT (bad) Sacked just once a game (good) Thrown for at least 3 TDs (uh, actually, really, really good) Now, if Stroud and the Texans could spin that into at least a 3-game or greater win streak…that would be even more helpful. 4813 : Days since the Houston Texans last won a game at “Reliant Stadium”. This stat has the caveat that after 2013, the Texans renamed Reliant to NRG. However, this past offseason, the Texans switched it back to Reliant. The last win at Reliant when it was Reliant: Sept 15, 2013, when the Texans came back to beat the Titans 30-24. This also snapped an 11-game losing streak at “Reliant”, as Houston lost the remaining 7 games in 2013 as well as the 1st 4 of the new “Reliant” era in 2026. GAME BALLS: RB David Montgomery: Since his 60 yard/2 TD rushing performance in Week 1, he’s only rushed for 78 yards and no TDs. This game was his first since Week 5. 26 carries for 107 yards (season highs for any Texans back in a game) and 3 receptions for 17 yards did quite nicely. How invaluable would this have been against the Browns in the second half? With a potentially treacherous road slate coming up, if Montgomery can run like this, Houston may yet have reason for hope. DE Will Anderson, Jr.: 5 Tackles/2 Solo/1 sack/2 TFLs/4 QB Hits/1 safety. Even without Danielle Hunter, Anderson almost single-handedly destroyed the Colts’ offense. RG Ed Ingram/RT Braden Smith: Maybe it was only a Colts’ squad playing out the string but consider: 83 of the Texans’ season-high 167 yards rushing came going to the offensive right, with the average rush going for over 5 yards/play. While a couple of the plays had Blake Fisher in as the extra blocker, the right side of the line was mainly Ingram and Smith. With winter coming, keeping up that high standard of play is a must. DE Chris Braswell : Gets elevated from the practice squad to the active roster with a chance to make something happen for a team that could use the help, and he gets injured on the opening kickoff. It won’t make up for the injury, but we’ll ship a game ball his way. SHOULD BE FORCED TO LISTEN TO CARLIE IRSAY-JORDAN’S GAME-DAY AUDIO AND HANDWRITE ON FANCY STATIONARY THE FULL TRANSCRIPT AFTER OVEREATING STALE TACO CABANA NACHOS : Houston’s Kickoff Coverage : Not everything was perfect in this game for the Texans. For the Texans, they did manage to give up a lot of yards on kickoff returns. Even on the opening kickoff, which could have been downed for a touchback to the IND 35, Colts RB/KR Seth McGowan ran it back for 40 yards, giving the Colts the ball in prime field position, allowing them to get that opening FG. McGowan gashed Houston for 117 yards on 3 kickoff returns. That put a lot of pressure on a mercurial defense. However, the defense did respond. Once McGowan left due to injury, the numbers worked out a little better, but this season has not been the best on the coverage front. Colts PK Spencer Shrader: A TDATDA Game Ball winner the last time these two met, it was the complete opposite this time. 1-of-3 on FGs, including a momentum-killing hook of a makable 56-yarder in the 1st quarter. With this win, Houston moves to 4-6, alone in second place in the AFC South and two games (effectively three) games back of the 7-seed Browns in the AFC. Houston gets an extended break before a defacto playoff game next Sunday against the struggling Ravens at Reliant. Kickoff slated for noon CST and can be seen on CBS/Paramount+

title: Stampede Blue Reacts results (Week 12): Colts fan confidence falls to 12% as frustration reaches new low
summary: According to this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, just 12 percent of Colts fans believe the team is headed in the right direction. That number marks another sharp drop in fan confidence and shows just how bleak things have become in Indianapolis. At this point, the overwhelming majority of the fan base appears to have […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon of the Indianapolis Colts takes the field prior to an NFL football game between the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, just 12 percent of Colts fans believe the team is headed in the right direction . That number marks another sharp drop in fan confidence and shows just how bleak things have become in Indianapolis. At this point, the overwhelming majority of the fan base appears to have little belief in the current direction of the franchise. The continued decline in confidence is hardly surprising. The Colts have spent the past several weeks spiraling, and whatever optimism may have briefly surfaced after some of the front office changes has quickly disappeared. Poor offensive play, frustrating coaching decisions and the overall lack of progress from week to week have left fans with very little reason to feel encouraged. Rather than showing signs of a team building toward something, Indianapolis has looked like a franchise stuck in the middle of a messy transition. The biggest recent development, of course, is that Daniel Jones is now gone, officially closing the book on a move that never gave the Colts the boost they were hoping for. Jones had a few respectable moments early on, but the offense became increasingly dysfunctional under his watch, and it eventually reached a point where a change simply had to be made. His departure does not solve all of Indianapolis’ problems, but it does signal that the organization recognized the situation was no longer tenable. Even so, the quarterback change alone is unlikely to restore confidence overnight. The issues with this team go far beyond one player. Shane Steichen continues to face questions about the offense, the roster still has major holes, and the Colts remain far away from looking like a legitimate contender. At the same time, fans are now left wondering whether this next phase will at least provide some clarity about the future, even if the short-term results remain ugly. For now, this week’s 12 percent confidence mark says it all. Colts fans are not just frustrated, they are increasingly unconvinced that this franchise has a real plan in place. If Indianapolis wants that number to rise in the coming weeks, it will need to show something far more convincing than it has lately. Does the Colts’ decision to release Daniel Jones give you more confidence in the franchise’s direction? FanDuel Sportsbook

summary: Today, the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) will take on the New York Giants (5-3-1) in Week 11. Giants head coach John Harbaugh had some bizarre comments about the Jaguars on Thursday. When asked about Jacksonville’s recent rise to becoming a top team, Harbaugh said he “could care less” (although he probably meant “couldn’t care less”). He could’ve taken […]
full_text: Oct 23, 2022; Jacksonville, Florida, USA; New York Giants cornerback Adoree' Jackson (22) hugs Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) at the end of the game at TIAA Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeremy Reper-USA TODAY Sports Today, the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) will take on the New York Giants (5-3-1) in Week 11. Giants head coach John Harbaugh had some bizarre comments about the Jaguars on Thursday. When asked about Jacksonville’s recent rise to becoming a top team, Harbaugh said he “could care less” (although he probably meant “couldn’t care less”). He could’ve taken the high road and said, “Yeah, they’re good, we’re in for a tough matchup,” and moved on. He quoted Bill Parcells instead. “It was interesting listening to Coach Harbaugh’s media,” Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Friday. “It’s like, yeah, you are what your record is, that’s a good thing. But any given Sunday—the NFL is the NFL. I was with the Rams in ‘22 when you lost to the 0-13 Jets. It is any given Sunday, anything can happen. And I do think our group believes that. They know that. I think they’re a little bit ticked, especially on the defensive side from some of the things that happened on Sunday that wasn’t up to our standard. So, I think when you have a hungry group that feels as if they have not done anything yet. Nothing. We’re in the second half of the season. A lot to prove, a lot of work, more games to be played than we even just did and went through. We have new additions now where this is our football team. This is an opportunity as we move forward throughout these next few weeks to go and put it on tape with this team, our final football team of who we are for the rest of the season. title: Jaguars vs. Giants: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 11
summary: Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! This week, we’re previewing the Jacksonville Jaguars’ matchup against the New York Giants in Week 11. Question 1: What’s your top question about the Jaguars this week? Dillon Appleman: Does Jordan Davis’ presence help the pass rush off the edge finally get home? Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker […]
full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) heads off the field after Sunday's loss to the New York Giants. The Jacksonville Jaguars hosted the New York Giants at TIAA Bank Field in Jacksonville, FL Sunday, October 23, 2022. The Jaguars trailed at the half 11 to 13 and lost to the Giants with a final score of 17 to 23. Jki 102322 Hsfb Bs Jaguars Vs Giants 20 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! This week, we’re previewing the Jacksonville Jaguars’ matchup against the New York Giants in Week 11. Question 1: What’s your top question about the Jaguars this week? Dillon Appleman : Does Jordan Davis’ presence help the pass rush off the edge finally get home? Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker have struggled to reach the quarterback this season, and some of it can be blamed on a lack of interior push that has allowed QBs the freedom to step up and avoid that outside pressure. We’ll see on Sunday if Davis’s push is enough to finally see a little more flash from the Jags’ expensive edge duo. Travis Holmes : Can this Jacksonville offensive line block the Giants’ defensive front one-on-one? As Liam Coen said on Monday, this game will be won in the trenches. When facing a Harbaugh team, of course it will. But Jacksonville will also have to stay out of obvious passing downs to avoid the clear problem areas. Walker Little and Cole Van Lanen against Kayvon Thibodeaux and Abdul Carter should be an interesting matchup, though Arvell Reese and his 4.5 sacks versus Ezra Cleveland, Emmanuel Pregnon, and Jonah Monheim is the one worth watching. Reese had a 3-sack game with a forced fumble against Philadelphia in Week 9, being used as an interior blitzer that forces teams to either play the Giants’ defensive line one-on-one or chip inside using running backs, where Reese normally has the athleticism advantage. As a top five blitzing team, that feels like something that may determine the game. Gus Logue : Will the weather make a difference? Rain is expected at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, so in theory, it could make the game a little sloppier and give the underdog a slight edge. On the other hand, Jacksonville scored 33 points against Baltimore and 42 points against Indianapolis in wet conditions in recent weeks. It’s probably nothing to be nervous about… but the turf at MetLife is a different beast. Henry Zimmer : My biggest question this week must be about how well and how much Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates play. This Giants offense is fine, but with two huge defensive additions for the Jags, it will be interesting to see how much they can impact a game already. Imagine a game where Bates gets a pick and Davis gets a sack. Question 2: What’s the key to a Jaguars victory this week? Dillon : The key is to end this fairy tale that J.J. McCarthy is in right now. After a brutal short career in Minnesota, McCarthy got dealt to the Giants this season and, to his credit, has played well in place of injured Jaxson Dart. That said, he’s faced nobody of substance since assuming the starting role. I’m looking for this Jacksonville defense to bring the McCarthy narrative down to earth a bit on Sunday. Travis : Jacksonville must find a way to eliminate the explosives in the passing game this week. J.J. McCarthy loves attacking deep more than any quarterback in the NFL. In his four games played, he’s first in air yards per attempt, both against the blitz and four-man rushes. But just looking at his overall resume, McCarthy is 22nd in the league in on-target throws (per SIS), right below Kyler Murray. In the deep passing game, the Jaguars have allowed 50% of opposing deep passes (20+ air yards) to be completed this year, the NFL’s fourth-worst rate. Meanwhile, the Giants rank top 10 with a 44.7% completion rate on deep passes. Jessie Bates should help in the deep middle, but the cornerbacks will still be challenged on the boundaries in this one. Gus : Don’t lose in the trenches. I don’t even think the Jaguars have to “win” there; they just can’t let the Giants build a significant advantage in that area. J.J. McCarthy doesn’t move me whatsoever. Between Travis Hunter and Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, Jacksonville should be equipped to contain Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely and Cam Skattebo, respectively. If the Giants put up enough points to keep pace with the Jaguars, I think it’s because they dominated in the trenches, not because of a sick performance by a skill position player. Henry : J.J. McCarthy has been throwing a ton of balls since he took over starting, but he only has 2 passing touchdowns. Limit McCarthy to yardage and no touchdowns and the Jags are winning their fourth straight. Question 3: Who will be an X-factor for the Jaguars this week ? Dillon : Chris Rodriguez. With Bhayshul Tuten still dealing with a lingering ankle injury, he may not be able to play Sunday. That means Rodriguez would get bell cow duties, and I’m confident he can step up if that is the case. The weather is looking bleak in East Rutherford on Sunday, which could lead to a sloppy run fest, so Rodriguez could be in line for a big role and will need to step up. Travis : Craig Wrolstad is this week’s X-factor in my book. If you don’t recognize that name, that makes sense. He’s the referee heading up this week’s officiating crew calling Sunday’s game. This is also the same crew that called Jacksonville’s Week 1 matchup against the Browns, where the Jaguars only had four penalties while Cleveland had 11. I only point that out because this crew ranks as the No. 1 officiating crew at calling defensive pass interference and No. 4 in illegal contact penalties, which may bode well for Jacksonville getting a few, since the Giants are already fifth in the league in DPI flags. Gus : I’m going to give a boring answer — Parker Washington — so I can give a cool stat. According to NFL Pro, Washington leads the league in yards per route run against press coverage (5.0) and on in-breaking routes (3.5). Both figures rank narrowly ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba. And New York’s defense aligns at least one cornerback in press coverage on a league-high 70.6% of snaps. Henry : My X-Factor this week is not a who but a what: the field surface at MetLife. This field is known for taking lives so I just hope that the Jags get away unscathed. This stadium scares the hell out of me. Final score prediction? Dillon : Jaguars 23, Giants 20 Travis : Jaguars 32, Giants 20 Gus : Jaguars 30, Giants 14 Henry : Jaguars 35, Giants 17 What are your Week 11 predictions, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments! title: Chiefs elevate 2 practice squad players for Week 11
summary: Ahead of Week 11’s home matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, the Kansas City Chiefs announced a pair of practice squad elevations for the contest. Running back Nate Carter and center Pete Nygra will get the nod on Sunday. As elevated players, they will immediately revert to the practice squad after the game. Second-year pro Carter […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Pete Nygra #50 of the Kansas City Chiefs lines up against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of a preseason game at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of Week 11’s home matchup against the Arizona Cardinals , the Kansas City Chiefs announced a pair of practice squad elevations for the contest. Running back Nate Carter and center Pete Nygra will get the nod on Sunday. As elevated players, they will immediately revert to the practice squad after the game. Second-year pro Carter made his Chiefs debut last week against the Atlanta Falcons as star running back Kenneth Walker sat with a groin injury. He carried the ball twice for six yards in relief of rookie Emmett Johnson, who finished the game with 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. Walker is ruled out again, but rookie running back Jadyn Ott has no game status after missing Week 10 with a hamstring injury. Assuming Ott is available to spell Johnson, Carter may only be an emergency option against Arizona. Nygra signed with Kansas City in April as an undrafted free agent out of Louisville. He has been a member of the practice squad the entire season after failing to make the final roster. Sunday will make Nygra’s NFL debut. Earlier this week, longtime Chiefs center — and current Sports Radio 810 WHB host — Tim Grunhard suggested that third-year pro Hunter Nourzad would start at right guard with starter Trey Smith in concussion protocol. Over three seasons, the Chiefs have seemed to view Nourzad as a center-specific backup while frequently bringing him in for six offensive lineman formations. Looks like Hunter Nourzad will start at RG for Trey Smith (concussion). Rooting for this young man… great kid! pic.twitter.com/WU1HL0uPsi — Tim Grunhard (@grunny61) November 21, 2026 Having another center in Nygra available would suggests merit to Grunhard’s report that Nourzad — and not Mike Caliendo — may truly get the start on Sunday. Also on Saturday, the Cardinals downgraded rookie quarterback Carson Beck to out with back spasms before departing to Kansas City. Beck had been listed as questionable on Friday after missing practice. 40-year-old Josh Johnson will officially start at quarterback against Kansas City on Sunday. Arizona also elevated veteran wideout Zay Jones from their practice squad.

title: Chiefs-Cardinals: 5 Things to Watch in Week 11 matchup
summary: The (7-2) Kansas City Chiefs will host the (3-7) Arizona Cardinals this week in an interconference matchup between AFC West and NFC West teams. The game kicks off at noon at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri, and will be broadcast on CBS. With a 35-13 blowout win over the Atlanta Falcons, the Chiefs found […]
full_text: Credit: Denny Medley-USA TODAY Sports The (7-2) Kansas City Chiefs will host the (3-7) Arizona Cardinals this week in an interconference matchup between AFC West and NFC West teams. The game kicks off at noon at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri, and will be broadcast on CBS . With a 35-13 blowout win over the Atlanta Falcons , the Chiefs found themselves back in the driver’s seat in the AFC West, taking a slight advantage over the Denver Broncos due to tiebreakers. The Cardinals found themselves on the opposite end of the stick, losing 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams to fall to dead last in their division. The Chiefs are heavy favorites heading into this week and need a win, with much tougher matchups on the horizon. Here are five things to watch : 1. The right side of the offensive line Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion) have been ruled out; Moore missed last week as well, and Smith went out in the first quarter. Josh Ezeudu will likely start his third game at right tackle, while Mike Caliendo should make his third start at right guard. Against the Falcons, the Chiefs’ offensive line issues didn’t matter, but they could limit how the offense calls plays. Patrick Mahomes and the skill players overcame the injuries up front last week, but it will be interesting to see whether Arizona targets the right side this week when the Chiefs drop back to pass. The Cardinals defense ranks 17th in the NFL in sacks this season with 17 total sacks. Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis was retained through the head coaching change from Jonathan Gannon to Mike LaFleur, and it will be interesting to see how he prepares to face the beat-up Chiefs offensive line. This alignment is more common now. Have seen the same look from Nick Rallis. https://t.co/fR3RZtaOqr — Chuck Harris (@chuckh3) November 17, 2026 This week, the Chiefs announced they signed veteran offensive tackle Fred Johnson to the team’s practice squad. Johnson has 22 career starts, so it will be interesting to see whether the team shifts the line further if performance issues arise or more injuries occur. Head coach Andy Reid commented on the line during his press conference on Friday. “Well, we’ve got a variety there, but they’re all going to have a shot to get in there and go, so we’ll see how it all goes,” Reid said. “But I think everybody has a lot of trust in Mike (Caliendo), if he’s the one in there playing.” 2. Improved pass rush Despite a slow start to the season, the Chiefs’ pass rush has delivered back-to-back solid performances, led by stars Chris Jones and George Karlaftis. Karlaftis leads the team with 5.5 sacks this season and has at least one in the last three games. Jones has three this year, but has come alive with 2.5 through the past two games. George Karlaftis is currently 10th in sacks among his position, & has the most QB hits as well. The Greek freak is 1st among all defensive linemen in passes batted down with 10, & 6th in pressures with 21. Last but not least, he’s 2nd in tackles for loss. Furious George is… pic.twitter.com/ja4iphE8pW — fatty patty (@theonlydyl_) November 18, 2026 The slow start getting home hurt the team, but both have played their best football so far in November. The sack that moved @StoneColdJones into 2nd all time in franchise history. pic.twitter.com/PrFapxFLpq — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 8, 2026 The defensive line has also seen the emergence of defensive end Ashton Gillotte, who has recorded at least one sack in the last two weeks, along with multiple pressures. Flea Flicker here gets blown up with the pressure from Gillotte. Does a good job of recognizing the play and out-leveraging the TE. Good inside hands and a strong long arm to get free. pic.twitter.com/bxTHJzKctb — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 9, 2026 The Cardinals have allowed 28 sacks so far this season, tied for sixth-worst in the NFL, and will start multiple backup-caliber players on their offensive line on Sunday. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck is unlikely to play, meaning journeyman backup Josh Johnson would start. If the Chiefs pass rush can turn in another solid performance, they should be able to shut down the Cardinals offense. 3. Increased role for Josh Downs General manager Brett Veach’s latest in-season acquisition started off his tenure in Kansas City on a positive note despite playing limited snaps and receiving only five targets against Atlanta. Post wheel action with Worthy pulling the safety. Downs with the double move to win the outside. 15 with a dart. pic.twitter.com/XMkfs2JKK8 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 15, 2026 In only ten snaps, Josh Downs caught four passes for 53 yards and hauled in an impressive touchdown to end the first half. In that limited action, he showed off his route-running ability and the sure hands needed in the Chiefs system. With a big game in the middle of next week against Buffalo, Downs likely won’t see every snap out wide, but I expect to see him get around 25-30 as he gets more comfortable in the Chiefs system. 4. Emmett Johnson In his first start, rookie running back Emmett Johnson exploded for a massive game, compiling 170 total yards on the ground and through the air and scoring two touchdowns off passes from Mahomes. With Kenneth Walker (groin) slated to miss his second consecutive game, Johnson will once again get the call to start. With the touchdowns, Johnson took the lead for rookie touchdowns and has moved himself into the conversation for the Offensive Rookie of the Year award. Most TDs scored among rookies this season Emmett Johnson 4 Denzel Boston 3 Jonah Coleman 3 11 players t-4 2 pic.twitter.com/LVgfQOvcJk — PFF (@PFF) November 15, 2026 Johnson has impressed with a tremendous combination of vision and cutting ability that has helped him find running lanes and break tackles at a high rate on so few touches. Most missed tackles forced among offensive rookies this season Emmett Johnson 28 Jadarian Price 15 Kaelon Black 14 Jonah Coleman 11 Seth McGowan 11 pic.twitter.com/py5Yhu2Y2M — PFF (@PFF) November 17, 2026 With 519 total scrimmage yards this season, Johnson has quickly become a difference-maker for the Chiefs offense, and even when Walker returns, Johnson should still see his role expand. I would expect to see Johnson in heavy doses on Sunday. 5. Delane and Williams The Chiefs have once again found elite cornerback play in Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams. A former third-round pick, Williams has quickly become one of the NFL’s best corners and has been among the league’s most effective players in man coverage. #Chiefs CB Nohl Williams against Falcons WR Drake London in Week 10: 10 matchups 1 target 0 receptions Williams did a remarkable job being physical to shut down one of the league's best. London wasn't charted as open once! The Chiefs have a rising star duo at CB 📈 pic.twitter.com/dG9RFxHcKj — Bradley Locker (@Bradley_Locker) November 16, 2026 Opposite Williams, Delane has been equally impressive and is making a run at a potential defensive rookie-of-the-year campaign. Critics questioned the decision to trade All-Pro corner Trent McDuffie in the offseason, but so far the trade has paid off. Delane and Williams are both on rookie deals and appear headed toward bright careers. Against a stumbling offense and a journeyman quarterback, this week will give each player a chance to pad their stats and look to add to their interception totals. Nohl Williams, a ball player. pic.twitter.com/OttDoF90gk — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) November 9, 2026

summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here. And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook, the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation. Chiefs fans’ confidence Playing against bad […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts , a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here . And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation. Chiefs fans’ confidence Playing against bad teams is a great way to build up your confidence in a team, and the Chiefs should continue their recent winning streak this week against the battered and lowly Arizona Cardinals , who are down to their third-string quarterback, Josh Johnson, and without star wide receiver Michael Wilson, who is out with an injured neck. This game is the perfect setup as the Chiefs head into their most important game of the season next week against the Buffalo Bills . Can the Chiefs still win the division? I think I have to agree with this poll. Aside from possibly Nohl Williams, no other defensive player has come close to being the impact player Karlaftis has been this season. Even when the sack numbers weren’t there, he has provided consistent pressure from the edge and batted more balls than Tony Gwynn in the 80s. The only argument against Karlaftis would be that he has feasted over these last couple of games by playing against lesser competition. But that’s what good players do: they beat up on mediocre opposition, and then they battle against the guys who are as good as they are. It’s only the true greats who dominate game in, game out. And while Karlaftis won’t even be the next Lawrence Taylor, he is still pretty good. Then again, if Karlaftis participated in the same pre-game rituals that Taylor did, maybe he’d play a little bit more like the crazed rhino Taylor was. But for the good of the team and the good of Karlaftis, we’ll say that good is good enough for now. Click here to see other recent survey results.

title: Chiefs-Cardinals: 5 questions with Revenge of the Birds ahead of Week 11
summary: On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Arizona Cardinals in the early afternoon slot of Week 11 games. We welcome Seth Cox of Revenge of the Birds— our sister SBNation site covering the Cardinals— for Five Questions with the Enemy. Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Revenge of […]
full_text: (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Arizona Cardinals in the early afternoon slot of Week 11 games. We welcome Seth Cox of Revenge of the Birds— our sister SBNation site covering the Cardinals— for Five Questions with the Enemy . Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Revenge of the Birds community through Sunday’s game to get perspectives from both sides of the Week 11 matchup! 1. Rookie Carson Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards with two interceptions and five sacks in his first NFL start. What would meaningful progress look like for Beck in his second start at Arrowhead? This may sound insane, but leading a touchdown drive. Since the miracle win against the Dallas Cowboys, the Arizona Cardinals have not scored a touchdown. They have three field goals. So, against the third ranked scoring defense, let’s just shoot for a touchdown and improving as a unit as they head into a more realistic schedule from a competitive standpoint after this debacle in Kansas City. There is also now a chance the Cardinals don’t even start Beck as he is dealing with back spasms. 2. Arizona has traded Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jacoby Brissett while describing the remainder of the season as an evaluation period. What have those decisions revealed about the direction general manager Monti Ossenfort and head coach Mike LaFleur are taking the franchise? Man, talk about an organization talking out of both sides of their mouth. The trade for Marv was after a complete dumpster fire to start the season for him, then they moved Brissett because he was benched and wanted out. Then the cavalcade of injuries has led to Josh Johnson likely starting a game in the year 2026 in the NFL. You had two veteran quarterbacks that would keep you competitive. You drafted a running back third overall because you needed to get a piece that fit what Mike LaFleur wanted to do on offense; you paid Trey McBride and Michael Wilson super high-end money because this wasn’t a rebuild. And within 10 weeks, it is not only a clear rebuild, but a complete teardown… except trading a 30-year-old safety on a bottom-three defense in the NFL. Nothing that has happened makes sense. 3. With Michael Wilson on injured reserve, Trey McBride has become the clear centerpiece of Arizona’s passing game with 78 receptions, 635 yards and five touchdowns. How can the Cardinals prevent Kansas City from taking away Beck’s most reliable target? McBride was always the focal point, but the injury to Wilson made him the only legitimate target. The Cardinals wide receivers remaining to throw to: Devin Duvernay – six receptions 57 yards Simi Fehoko – two receptions 38 yards Harrison Wallace – one reception nine yards Reggie Virgil – three receptions 54 yards Zay Jones – no catches no yards The Cardinals entire wide receiver room for the season: 12 receptions 158 yards Those are not the stats for last week, those are for the entire season. So, it’ll be a lot of Trey McBride, but the Rams and Seahawks have put the gameplan out on letting him get receptions and not gaining yards. And now it could be Josh Johnson starting… yay! 4. The Cardinals rank 31st in points allowed and surrendered 436 total yards, including 202 rushing yards, against the Rams. What is the biggest weakness in Arizona’s defense that the Chiefs are equipped to exploit? Being on the field? They seem to be okay covering, but they are terrible at rushing the passer, and covering for four seconds in the NFL is not ideal. They cannot stop the run, but I genuinely think Emmett Johnson may not be needed as much because the Chiefs will likely be up by so much. The Chiefs will be able to throw the ball if they want, run the ball if they want, score as much as they want. It will be a complete cluster on Sunday. 5. What is your prediction for how Sunday’s game unfolds, including the final score? The Cardinals have not scored a touchdown in two games. I don’t see that changing with Josh Johnson as the quarterback after just 10 days with the team. Chiefs 31, Cardinals 6 Good luck and good health to the Chiefs in this one.

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news With Carson Beck injured, Cardinals preparing to start fourth different QB in 4 weeks | The Athletic In a Friday appearance on the “Wolf & Luke Show,” general manager Monti Ossenfort said Beck suffered back spasms about halfway through Thursday’s practice. The Cardinals limited Beck the rest of the session and held him out of Friday’s workout. Carson dealt with this a little bit earlier in the season, and in his role at the time, we were very safe with what we asked him to do and took our time with it. We’ll see how it goes here.” NFL Makes Announcement on Chiefs Rookie Emmett Johnson | Yahoo! Sports The NFL announced that Emmett Johnson has won its weekly honor. The league also uploaded a video of his Week 10 highlights on Instagram. @emmettj_ is the Week 10 @pepsi Rookie of the Week Johnson has outplayed his draft status and making a name for himself as a rising star. Kansas City will continue to rely on him as the season progresses, especially with his ability to contribute as a running back and receiver. Injuries to Drake Maye and Puka Nacua Lighten the Challenge of the Chiefs’ Upcoming Gauntlet | Sports Illustrated Without Maye, New England’s offense is led by backup quarterback Tommy DeVito—an obvious downgrade for the 5-5 Patriots. Meanwhile, Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua certainly won’t be on the field against the Chiefs in Los Angeles one week after Thanksgiving due to an injury and suspension. Without getting into the details of the (injury/suspension) designation, the already-injury-riddled Rams will be missing at least one key weapon when they host KC. Veteran receiver Davante Adams could potentially return in time to face the Chiefs, but that’s far from a certainty. On the defensive side of the ball, former Chiefs cornerback Jaylen Watson has been ruled out for the rest of the year due to a shoulder injury. Recalling some great moments in Arrowhead Stadium history as Chiefs prep for move | The Kansas City Star Some top moments since the venue opened in 1972: The most unforgettable game in Arrowhead history came on Jan. 23, 2022, when Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes hit Travis Kelce for an 8-yard overtime touchdown to beat the Buffalo Bills 42-36 in the AFC Divisional Round — a finish that later won an ESPY as ESPN’s “Game of the Year.” The venerable stadium just east of downtown also set a Guinness World Record in 2014, when crowd noise hit 142.2 decibels during the Chiefs’ “Monday Night Football” rout of the New England Patriots. Chiefs’ Trey Smith helps distribute 400 Thanksgiving meals to Kansas City families | KMBC 9 Five players who are not working L’Jarius Sneed, CB, Chiefs How he got there: Signed a one-year, $1.2 million contract (up to $5 million in incentives) 2026 stat to know: 128.3% coverage DVOA (not enough snaps to qualify but higher is worse) Comparable 2025 stat: 10.8% coverage DVOA The Chiefs turned over almost their entire secondary this offseason and have gotten a lot of value out of second-year corner Nohl Williams and first-round rookie Mansoor Delane. But they brought back Sneed, a key player on their back-to-back Super Bowl-winning teams in 2022 and 2023, to play in the slot. That hasn’t worked out as well. Around the NF L Colts waive QB Daniel Jones in puzzling cap move, turn to Anthony Richardson in Week 12 | The Athletic Jones, 29, has struggled all season, throwing 13 interceptions to just seven touchdowns in 11 games while completing a career-low 58.4 percent of his passes. The Colts (3-8) have lost six of their past seven games. Their decision to cut Jones now will result in a $35.2 million dead cap hit for the 2027 season — a figure that could have been significantly reduced had the Colts simply benched him and waited to cut him in March. Patriots WR A.J. Brown expected to miss multiple weeks due to hamstring injury, per report | CBS Sports Brown suffered the hamstring injury during their Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Germany. The 29-year-old has dealt with numerous injuries this season, finding himself on the injury report more times than not. The three-time Pro Bowler suffered an ankle injury in their season opener and was placed on injured reserve, missing four games. After he returned, he then missed two games due to a knee strain. NFL will consider requiring minimum-night stays for international games | Pro Football Talk “Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club,” NFL executive V.P. of club business, major events, and international Peter O’Reilly told The Athletic . “It is something that we’ll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It’s something we’ll look at.” The league already does it for the Super Bowl, mandating a full-week experience that includes multiple press conferences, the annual “Opening Night” media extravaganza, and practicing at designated facilities. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Have the Chiefs finally fixed their pass rush? Brandon Thorn of Establish the Run is as respected as any offensive line analyst covering the game, and he currently has the Jets ranked as his 12th-best offensive line in the league. He has the Falcons at 19th. Not world beaters, but this wasn’t the Chiefs taking advantage of the early-season Packers MASH unit offensive line. This weekend should set up well for another dominant performance by the Chiefs’ D-Line. The Cardinals’ quarterbacks have been sacked 8 times over the past two weeks. Thorn ranks their offensive line as the third worst in the league. This could be yet another get-right game for the defensive side of the ball before things start to get real. title: Puka Nacua’s Rams career over? ESPN report says yes
summary: Puka Nacua’s career with the Los Angeles Rams has “probably ended”, according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. But that report feels speculative, uninformed, and flat-out ignorant by Fowler. The Rams will let Nacua leave in free agency? That seems ridiculously unlikely. Players of Nacua’s age and ability are rarely allowed to hit free agency and no […]
full_text: Puka Nacua’s career with the Los Angeles Rams has “probably ended”, according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. But that report feels speculative, uninformed, and flat-out ignorant by Fowler. The Rams will let Nacua leave in free agency? That seems ridiculously unlikely. Players of Nacua’s age and ability are rarely allowed to hit free agency and no matter what the situation is on Puka’s side or L.A.‘s side with a long list of free agents and needs, the Rams would sooner franchise tag the receiver than let him walk for a third-round compensatory pick in 2028. Nacua is worth at least two first-round picks, and the Rams know it. “Up in the air as it pertains to his future with the Rams. Going into free agency, he has two significant injuries, including an MCL injury that Sean McVay says will keep him out a few months ago. Probably ends his tenure with the Rams,” says Fowler. Jeremy Fowler on Puka Nucua’s future: the injury/suspension “probably ends his tenure with the Rams.” Nucua is set to become a free agent this coming spring. pic.twitter.com/rrexUCCnbP — uSTADIUM (@uSTADIUM) November 21, 2026 Jeremy Fowler is typically a solid reporter, so it’s hard to fathom why he would go to the lengths of saying that Nacua’s career with the Rams is “probably over” while in the next breath acknowledging that Nacua is the best free agent of 2027. The “best free agent” next year is never a free agent. Although the Rams have challenging test ahead for Les Snead when it comes to their free agents and budget , keeping Nacua — or at least tagging him — is non-negotiable. Snead will not let Nacua leave “in free agency” like Fowler says under any circumstances, unless pigs fly by March. The only rational way that Nacua’s career ends is if the Rams tag him and he is traded for at least a first and a second-round pick, if not better. That will also be tough for L.A. to manage given the complexity of trades of that magnitude and the need to find a team that is not only willing to pay Nacua like a top-tier receiver, but also sacrifice the draft picks to complete a deal. Hypothetically let’s say that the Raiders want to trade for Nacua and Las Vegas is holding pick 10. Will the Raiders be willing to trade pick 10 and pick 42 and pay Nacua a four-year, $170 million contract? If there’s any team willing to do that it would be the Raiders, but Las Vegas is under new management and Tom Brady may not be so quick to rush a deal like that for Nacua. The likelier scenario? The Rams, Nacua find a way As bad as things look now, the fact is that Nacua is the best player on the Rams and this is a roster that is about to get a whole lot less talented in 2027 if Matthew Stafford and Davante Adams and Aaron Donald retire/walk away. What star power is left? Ty Simpson and Konata Mumpfield? Unless the Rams want to do a full blown rebuild — which may not be a bad idea — then Nacua should stay and get the contract he deserves. Even if the Rams do rebuild, who is Simpson supposed to be developing as a quarterback with? Mumpfield and C.J. Daniels? Seriously? Fowler says Nacua’s career with the Rams is probably over. I say that’s probably a shortsighted overreaction.

title: Sportsbooks favor the Rams to make the playoffs
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are currently on the outside looking in when it comes to the NFL playoffs. In the NFC, the Rams are currently ninth while only the top seven seeds make the postseason. But while some media outlets currently say Los Angeles is an underdog to reach the postseason, one notable source is […]
full_text: (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are currently on the outside looking in when it comes to the NFL playoffs. In the NFC, the Rams are currently ninth while only the top seven seeds make the postseason. But while some media outlets currently say Los Angeles is an underdog to reach the postseason, one notable source is giving them more than a puncher’s chance: sportsbooks. While the Rams are in the middle of their sort-of-not-really bye week, they’ll be focused intently a couple of games that could shift the playoff odds around the NFC. Obviously, they need to just keep winning to further solidify their status. ~~WEEK 11 NFC PLAYOFF LEVERAGE~~ A week 11 SNF game to determine the No. 1 seed sounds crazy, but wow 49ers-Vikings is an enormous game. Hopefully it's a better game than CIN-PIT was pic.twitter.com/TMmXC1galX — Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) November 18, 2026 More than anything, though, this is implying that gamblers are more confident in the Rams than some of their peer teams in the NFC playoff race, specifically thinking of the Green Bay Packers. How convenient that the Rams play the Packers in Week 12. According to FanDuel , the current price for a bet on the Rams to make the playoffs is -116. That means the implied odds of Los Angeles being postseason bound is 53.7%. It’s even more noticeable at DraftKings , where the Rams are currently sitting at -128 to make the playoffs, or a 56.1% implied probability. If you enjoy gambling and prefer a different book, that’s fine, because seemingly across the board, the gambling world thinks more highly of the Rams as a playoff team than their counterparts. The Los Angeles Rams were 2-4. Then 3-4. Then 4-4. Then 5-4. Then 6-4. Y’all buried them too soon. — Sam Block (@theblockspot) November 15, 2026 Compare that to some of the other predictive sources and you see a different story. According to NFL.com , L.A. currently only has a 47% chance to make the postseason (still ahead of Green Bay, for what it’s worth). The Athletic and its playoff predictor give the Rams the same chance. The venerable PlayoffStatus.com is even more bearish on the Rams, setting their current playoff likelihood at 41%. You get the gist. It’s fairly easy to understand the disparity between the gambling houses and the current math. While both are trying to predict the future, only one can account for the return of Myles Garrett, an increasingly more comfortable Aaron Donald and a Matthew Stafford who is finally starting to push the ball more . The traditional models don’t include the same kind of context. Aaron Donald looks and sounds like a player who got to play with Myles Garrett today 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/WG2BA4Sw8z — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 8, 2026 It goes without saying that nothing can perfectly predict what will unfold for the Rams and their playoff chances down the home stretch of the season, and that the best recipe for playing deep into January (and maybe later) is to simply win more games now. Still, the oddsmakers like the Rams. Or at least, they like the Rams a bit more than their closest competition.

title: With no Rams game, who are you rooting for?
summary: While it has been another gripping week for Los Angeles Rams fans, the Week 11 bye offers both the team and its fans a brief respite until Thanksgiving Eve potboiler. That’s when the Green Bay Packers take to steed from the frozen tundra of the North, marauding west into the City of Angels. How L.A. […]
full_text: While it has been another gripping week for Los Angeles Rams fans, the Week 11 bye offers both the team and its fans a brief respite until Thanksgiving Eve potboiler. That’s when the Green Bay Packers take to steed from the frozen tundra of the North, marauding west into the City of Angels. How L.A. handles this battle will be the harbinger for a stretch of games, with all games bigger than the previous. There could be nothing better than the Rams gaining ground in the playoff race while on a day off. There are three games this Sunday that have some meaning to L.A. fans. Get down on the rail and root them home. Here’s how to follow these three important games. New Orleans Saints (3-6) @ Chicago Bears (7-2) Kickoff: 10 a.m. PST Location: Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois Network TV broadcast: FOX Play-by-play: Kevin Burkhardt Color analyst: Tom Brady Sideline reporters: Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi To keep it simple, Rams fans can clearly root against the NFC North every week over the final eight weeks. The Bears, Lions, Packers, and Vikings are all within reach and surmountable. This one’s a long shot. The weather will be rather mild for this time of year, 58 degrees, with morning rain that may linger after kickoff. A wet track favors Chicago, they lead the NFL in run attempts and rushing yards per game, while New Orleans languishes in the Bottom 10 defending the ground attack. Although two the Saints three wins have come on the road, their offense is plodding, particularly the run game. It won’t help that three starting offensive linemen are out. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) @ Detroit Lions (7-2) Kickoff: 10 a.m. PST Location: Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan Network TV broadcast: FOX Play-by-play: Kevin Kugler Color analyst: Daryl Johnston Sideline reporter: Allison Williams The Lions are 5-0 at thus far and have already banked victories over division rivals Minnesota and Detroit. They could get caught looking past the Bucs, with their eyes on a big Week 12 home meeting with the Chicago Bears. All six of Tampa Bay’s losses have come by seven points or less. The Buccaneers have one the top rushing offenses in the league, but rank at the bottom in passing. They like to to make full use of the clock, most seconds per play (2nd), time of possession (3rd), and time of possession percentage (3rd). Detroit has fairly balanced offense (55% pass), but likes the chunk plays, they land fourth in explosive plays. Minnesota Vikings (7-2) vs San Francisco 49ers (8-1) Kickoff: 5:20 p.m. PST Location: Estadio Banorte in Mexico City, Mexico Network TV broadcast: NBC Play-by-play: Mike Terico Color analyst: Cris Collinsworth Sideline reporter: Melissa Stark No matter how this game falls, the Rams gain ground on a squad ahead of them. I get it, rooting for the ‘Niners is like a snake eating a porcupine, only once a lifetime and you have to be in dire straits. West coast rivalry aside, the Vikes have a fairly soft schedule after Sunday. It seems prudent to root for them to beat up on San Francisco and then later on their division rivals, Detroit and Chicago. San Francisco has been an offensive machine so far and trending up, 400 yards or better and 33 points per game over three straight outings. The defense is salty against the run, but is below the midline stopping the pass. Minnesota’s blitzing defense had carried the team and its lack of competent quarterback play. Now that Kirk Cousins is at the throttle, the offense might be able to pull its own weight.

title: Should the Rams have added a wide receiver?
summary: Should the Los Angeles Rams have a traded for a wide receiver at the trade deadline with Puka Nacua expected to be out? Was anyone available going to replace Nacua? Likely not. Nacua’s injury is a loss to the Rams no matter who they could’ve added via trade. Will the Rams be able to overcome […]
full_text: Should the Los Angeles Rams have a traded for a wide receiver at the trade deadline with Puka Nacua expected to be out? Was anyone available going to replace Nacua? Likely not. Nacua’s injury is a loss to the Rams no matter who they could’ve added via trade. Will the Rams be able to overcome the loss of Nacua? Anything can happen, but likely not exactly. Nacua offered an incredible offensive presence and he’s out now. There is no easy answer. The Rams will just have to put in the work and play their best. Will it be enough? They’ll find out. Rams WR Puka Nacua had MCL surgery, likely to miss rest of season (ramswire) “McVay says he will miss a couple of months, which means he probably won’t play again this season. Initially, Nacua was placed on IR but was expected to return in mid-December after missing the minimum of four games. But that was before the Rams realized he needed surgery, which will prolong his rehab. Nacua is scheduled to be a free agent in March. “Puka Nacua decided to get surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, so that’ll be a couple of months for him,” McVay said.“ Injury Updates: Puka Nacua out for ‘couple months’ as he will undergo MCL surgery; Kobie Turner expected to return to practice; latest on Terrance Ferguson, Davante Adams and Justin Dedich (therams.com) ‘Additionally, defensive end Kobie Turner is expected to return to practice and the Rams will open his 21-day practice window this week after sustaining a Week 6 groin injury that landed him on Injured Reserve. McVay added, “hopefully he’ll be ready to go this week.” With regard to tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) and wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring)’s potential returns in Week 12, McVay said “we’re not quite there yet.” After an ankle injury in Week 4 led to the Rams placing Ferguson on IR, he started his 21-day practice window in the week leading up to Week 9, but picked up a hamstring injury during the Friday practice before the Commanders game. Ferguson missed Week 9 and Week 10 before the bye week. McVay said the plan is to still bring Ferguson onto the active roster before that 21-day window closes so he doesn’t have to be shut down for the season.“ Rams WR Puka Nacua has knee surgery, likely out for season, McVay says (spectrumnews1) “McVay had expressed optimism last week that Nacua could return to the field this season, but he said the star wideout decided this week to have surgery, which was performed Tuesday. Nacua is in the final year of his rookie contract and is eligible to sign a large extension. “I kind of thought when the initial injury occurred that this was more likely the direction that this would go, so this isn’t anything necessarily new on our end,” McVay said. “He had to get some different information, talk to people, and there’s a lot of conversations that go into whether you’re going to do that or not, and what’s the best plan of action for return to performance for him — not exclusive to this year, but for his career moving forward.” Nacua received a three-game suspension from the NFL on Thursday for violating its personal conduct policies. His suspension will expire during his mandated four-game stint on injured reserve, but the knee surgery will keep him out much longer.“ Packers Catch Huge Break Ahead of Must-Win Rams Showdown (sports.yahoo) “The Packers’ loss to the Vikings dropped their playoff odds to just 35 percent, and Green Bay’s next game, which comes against the Los Angeles Rams on November 25, will determine whether the Packers’ chances at a fourth consecutive trip to the postseason spike to 58 percent or plummet to 23 percent. That doesn’t necessarily render Green Bay’s return to the gridiron five days from now a must-win, but the path to the playoffs gets murky with a loss to the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve — not only because it will drop the Packers to 6-5 and take the division almost entirely out of play, but because the Rams are likely to prove prime competition for one of the last wildcard spots in the NFC and will hold the head-to-head tiebreaker with a victory.“ Rams WR Puka Nacua has surgery on MCL and is likely OUT for the 2026 season | ‘The NFL Report’ (nfl.com) “Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua had surgery to repair an MCL and will likely miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season.” Rams should have all the convincing they need to commit to CJ Daniels (ramblinfan) “Even with Adams back, the Rams can no longer treat Daniels as a placeholder to be discarded upon Nacua’s return. Instead, they have every reason to continue his development in earnest for the remainder of the season. Rams have little to lose by doubling down on CJ Daniels Despite flashes from veteran Tutu Atwell and a team-leading Week 10 performance from Konata Mumpfield , the Rams have not gotten consistent contributions beneath Adams and Nacua on the receiver depth chart. Disappointingly, Atwell has been plagued by a bout of drops.“ One questionable play call may have crushed Rams’ Super Bowl chances (ramswire) “ McVay even admitted a day after the game that he was “kicking” himself for that play call and has questioned the decision “over and over,” knowing the consequences of losing Nacua. That was almost two weeks ago, before the Rams knew Nacua needed surgery. “I’m kicking myself about those things,” he said. “… I’d be lying to you if I said I haven’t questioned the decision making on that last play over and over in my head of what could have been another option that you felt like could have gotten a conversion and maybe end of the game that would have led to him not taking a violent hit to his right knee. It’s stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for, and we have to be able to figure out how to protect these guys while also putting them in positions that help our team and allow them to be able to shine.” Sean McVay discusses injury updates, evolving the Rams’ offense, preparing for Week 12 & more (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay discusses injury updates, continuing to evolve the Rams’ offense, preparing for Week 12 against the Green Bay Packers, and more.” Puka Nacua Injury Exposes Rams’ Biggest Roster Management Failure (si.com) “Ferguson couldn’t make it through one full practice after the Rams opened his practice window before injuring his hamstring. Adams underwent surgery on his hamstring, but it’s the same one that has bothered him for the last two years It’s always easy to look at roster decisions with the benefit of hindsight. With that said, depth at the wide receiver position is something that the Rams have needed since the early spring. Rams’ Failure to Address Wide Receiver Depth Was Always a Risk Ignoring the position and banking on injury-prone players to stay healthy always felt like roster mismanagement. Now, the Rams are set to enter the hardest part of their schedule and will be relying on players like Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith, and CJ Daniels.“ Seahawks Dealt Favorable Rams Twist in NFC West Race: Insider (nfl.com) “Asked whether the receiver’s regular season was over, McVay said, “You can pretty much say yes.” Jeremiah looked at the schedule during an appearance on “The Rich Eisen Show” . Seattle still has both games against Los Angeles ahead of it. “They’re not gonna have to deal with Puka twice,” Jeremiah said. “They’re the biggest winners in this whole thing.” Comment of the day: Feed post of the day:
author: Danny Stone

title: Has Bo Nix quieted early-season criticisms ahead of Las Vegas Raiders-Denver Broncos Week 11 matchup?
summary: Week 11 reignites a longstanding AFC West rivalry between the Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos. To preview the game, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our frenemies at Mile High Report, and Ian St. Clair was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Broncos for Raider Nation. Q: Bo Nix faced […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 11 reignites a longstanding AFC West rivalry between the Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos . To preview the game, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our frenemies at Mile High Report, and Ian St. Clair was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Broncos for Raider Nation. Q: Bo Nix faced a lot of criticism at the beginning of the season for not pushing the ball down the field. Has that changed over the last handful of games? Is ending last season with a broken ankle impacting how he’s been playing in 2026? A: No matter what happens on the field, Nix is one of those players who will always face criticism. It’s also important to add some context for why things may unfold on the field over the course of a game. Early in the season, Nix and the Broncos offense played some of the best defenses in the NFL. On top of that, Denver’s running game was horrendous, and that’s even putting it mildly. Opposing defenses knew they could stop the Broncos rushing attack with minimal effort and play two-high safeties. In situations like that, it’s going to be hard for a quarterback or offense to push the ball down the field. However, Nix and Denver did open it up a bit more against the Carolina Panthers. Early in the game, Nix took some deep shots that set up the offense for points. We will likely see a continuation of that this Sunday. As for Nix’s injury, there’s no doubt it impacted him earlier in the season. I’d say more so mentally than physically. All the physical rehab in the world doesn’t rehab the mind until you actually do it and prove to yourself that you can do it. The last few games have been more like the Nix we saw before the injury, and belief and confidence are reemerging. Q: On a related note, Jaylen Waddle was the Broncos’ biggest offseason addition but has just 30 catches for 337 yards and two touchdowns through nine games. What were the expectations for Waddle heading into the season, and what’s been holding him back from meeting them? A: The expectations were high that Waddle would bring an element to Denver’s offense that would open it up. Nix and the Broncos would be able to take deep shots and use his speed in the middle of the field. It’s been surprising how inconsistent that has been thus far. We’ve seen flashes, but not nearly enough. Obviously, what I mentioned earlier with the focus opposing defenses can put on the passing game plays into that, but it’s also not utilizing him properly. Plus, the fact that Nix has been inconsistent and struggled hasn’t helped. Coming out of the bye, I think we’ll start to see Waddle play a bigger role in the Broncos offense. Q: Who would you say is more important to Denver’s defense and why: Nik Bonitto or Pat Surtain II? A: My answer might change in five minutes, but I’ll go with Bonitto. Mind you, I think that Surtain is the best cornerback in football. He’s one of those cornerbacks who shuts down half the field. However, having a game-changing edge rusher in Bonitto sets the rest of the defense up for success, including Surtain. What Bonitto brings and how effective he is reminds me of Von Miller, who was the Super Bowl 50 MVP. At any moment, Bonitto can make a play that changes a game. Or, in the case against the Panthers, win it. He’s become one of the best edge players in the league, and he just brings so much to the Broncos’ defense. Q: Seahawks head coach/defensive play caller Mike Macdonald gave Fernando Mendoza trouble last week by throwing the book at the rookie with several exotic pressure looks. Should Mendoza expect the same from Vance Joseph this week? What can you tell us about Joseph’s scheme that could give a quarterback making his second career start fits? A: The scheme is only as good as the players who execute it, and that’s where I think Mendoza will face similar challenges this Sunday. Denver is one of the best defenses in the NFL, if not the best, at pressuring the quarterback. Even if Joseph doesn’t call a blitz, the Broncos front will still make life miserable for Mendoza with Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, Zack Allen, and Co. But then there are the times Joseph will send a cornerback or safety on a blitz out of package that Mendoza isn’t expecting. But the biggest reason Mendoza will face pressure is the Raiders’ currently ineffective running game. Being one-dimensional on offense is never a friend to a rookie quarterback making his second start against a great defense. Q: Can you give us one player on each side of the ball who Raider Nation might not know much about but could make an impact in this game? A couple of the Broncos’ up-and-comers, if you will . A: On offense, let’s go with rookie running back Jonah Coleman. Though I’m pretty sure Las Vegas fans know of Coleman. But he is what makes Denver’s running game click. Coleman’s has good vision, good speed, and runs with power. He’s been fun to watch, and I would expect him to get more carries on Sunday. On defense, there really isn’t anybody who Raiders Nation hasn’t heard of. So I’ll go with cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian. The fourth-year undrafted defensive back has a knack for making a key play when Denver needs it, whether an interception or a sack.

title: Division games a true barometer of Raiders progress, or lack of it
summary: Divisional games just hit different in the NFL. Featuring the twice-a-year meetings which lead to some heated rematches, the weight division games carry are much heavier than the standard affair of matchups league schedule makers put forth amongst the 32 teams. When the AFC and NFC teams in the East, North, South, and West tango, […]
full_text: (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Divisional games just hit different in the NFL. Featuring the twice-a-year meetings which lead to some heated rematches, the weight division games carry are much heavier than the standard affair of matchups league schedule makers put forth amongst the 32 teams. When the AFC and NFC teams in the East, North, South, and West tango, the playoff stakes are higher (I’ll explain this more below) alongside familiarity creating either nail-biter meetings lopsided beatdowns. It’ll be intriguing to see which way the Las Vegas Raiders road trip to the Denver Broncos this Sunday plays out. Will it be an AFC West slugfest that’s close? Or will the bucking Broncos trample the visiting Raiders? With four of the final seven games on Las Vegas’ slate being AFC West tilts — at Denver this Sunday; hosting the Los Angeles Chargers (Week 14, Dec. 13); hosting the Broncos (Week 15, Dec. 20); and at the Kansas City Chiefs (Week 18, Jan. 10) — we’re going to see how much progress Klint Kubiak’s Raiders have made — or the lack of it. Kubiak, the heralded offensive mind who the Silver & Black tabbed as its 27th head coach in franchise history, has a storied history with Denver as he grew up around the team thanks to his father Gary, who spent decades as a Broncos player, offensive coordinator, head coach, and senior personnel advisory. “Yeah, many memories. Looking forward to going back to the stadium and being a part of this game. Extremely excited for our team,” the stoic younger Klint Kubiak said when asked about a memory that stands out as he heads back to Denver, this time, as a rookie head coach. “I think when I was blessed enough to get hired here to coach the Raiders, I thought about games in Denver and games in Kansas City and being a part of this division, so it’s something that I’ve definitely thought about before. And now that we’re in it, we’re in the season. It’s just next practice.” Kubiak is set to lead his 4-6 Raiders against Sean Peyton’s 7-2 Broncos highlighting the different spectrums of success the two division foes are currently at. A win keeps Denver in-line with the 7-2 Chiefs and an all-important AFC West title and high seed in the postseason race. A victory by Las Vegas puts a nice shiner on Denver’s division title hunt. "They always show up and play the Broncos hard." 🗣️ Courtland Sutton on facing Klint Kubiak and the @Raiders #broncoscountry pic.twitter.com/PhCfC2g1p5 — Guerilla Sports (@guerillasports) November 19, 2026 As Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton aptly mentioned above, the division games often lead to close, hard-fought one-score contests because teams know each other so well that tendencies are identified and counters properly installed. Even when one team is the cellar desperately trying to climb out, it can give a team atop the mountain with lofty goals in their eyes a difficult time gameday. This is a direct result of that deep familiarity and competitive drive amongst players and coaches. As they say, familiarity breeds contempt and there’s no love lost between the Raiders and Broncos — heck, the entire AFC West. Las Vegas intends to be in the spot Denver is now — fighting for the division crown, a ticket to the postseason dance, and a legitimate chase for another Lombardi Trophy — and the future is now as the team traded trusty veteran Kirk Cousins and are now on the Fernando Mendoza era at quarterback. The rookie and No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft is well aware of what Week 11 presents for the Silver & Black. “It’s a great challenge. It’s a rivalry game. If you can’t get excited for a rivalry game, then there might be something wrong with you,” Mendoza said. “So, I’m incredibly excited to take on the challenge. They’re a great opponent. They have a great team. They have a great coach and a great quarterback. So, I’m looking forward to taking it on with my teammates.” Through the 10 games the Raiders have played this season, the team is 1-1 in AFC West play (beat the Chargers 26-14 in Week 2; lost to the Chiefs 30-27 in Week 4) and are 3-3 against AFC foes. The Broncos, on the other hand, are coming off their bye week and are 2-1 in division games played (lost the Chiefs 31-10 in Week 1; beat the Chargers 23-17 in Week 5, topped the Chiefs 28-24 in Week 8) and are 3-1 in AFC play through their nine games on the year. I hate the fact I don’t hate the @Raiders with the same hate I once hated the @Raiders . pic.twitter.com/IpBCVTDkLJ — Vic Lombardi (@VicLombardi) November 16, 2026 Kubiak needs to get complementary football from his Raiders where his offense combines with Rob Leonard’s defense, and Joe DeCamillis’ special teams unit to lift each unit up against a Broncos team eyeing back-to-back AFC West titles, something the Chiefs won nine-straight seasons from 2016-2024. “Yeah, absolutely. Obviously, I’ve learned how big of an operation this is, and how it takes a team to go win a football game,” Kubiak said on what he’s learned about himself 10 games into his head coaching career. “It’s every week I’m learning new things. But the great thing about this whole experience is surrounding yourself with excellent people, and from our personnel staff to our coaching staff to our players, I could not have come into a better situation with the type of people.” Sunday marks a first for Mendoza, too. “Yeah, it’s going to be very loud. They have a great fan base, and that’s something we’ve been practicing at practice, whether it’s the crowd noise, to make sure we get adjusted to that. It’s going to be a great environment,” the rookie said. “But it is new. I’ve never started on the road before, so I’m looking forward to the challenge.” Quotes of Note “Protection is an all 11 thing. It’s everybody. The run game is an all 11 thing. That’s the greatest thing about football; is every play all 11 people are involved. It’s not just one person making a play. It’s all 11 coming together for success. So, everybody has a role in a touchdown play. Everybody has a role in a sack. Everybody has a role in an explosive run. Everybody has a role in a tackle for loss. So, specifically, you look at each individual play and you coach every single position on how can we get better in that circumstance to make that play successful.” —Las Vegas Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko on the shared responsibility of accounting for cornerback blitzes “Yeah, at times. We’re not playing well enough. We’re not playing up to the standard we need to be. So, effort covers up a lot. So, there’s definitely room for improvement there. And to say it’s division from the start, no, we’re not playing at a high enough or good enough level right now. So, there’s definitely room for improvement.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard on how the fast and aggressive play style he wants from his defenders has translated into game days
